title.zh: 卷84 儒林:梁越 盧醜 張偉 梁祚 平恆 陳奇 常爽 劉獻之
title.en: Volume 84: Renowned Confucians - Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Chang Shuang, Liu Xianzhi
title.raw: 卷84 儒林:梁越 盧醜 張偉 梁祚 平恆 陳奇 常爽 劉獻之 Volume 84: Renowned Confucians - Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Chang Shuang, Liu Xianzhi

sentences.zh: 梁越 盧醜 張偉 梁祚 平恒 陳奇 常爽 劉獻之 張吾貴 劉蘭 孫惠蔚 徐遵明 董徵 刁沖 盧景裕 李同軌 李業興

translations.literal: Liang Yue; Lu Chou; Zhang Wei; Liang Zuo; Ping Heng; Chen Qi; Chang Shuang; Liu Xianzhi; Zhang Wugui; Liu Lan; Sun Huiwei; Xu Zunming; Dong Zheng; Diao Chong; Lu Jingyu; Li Tonggui; Li Yexing
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yue; Lu Chou; Zhang Wei; Liang Zuo; Ping Heng; Chen Qi; Chang Shuang; Liu Xianzhi; Zhang Wugui; Liu Lan; Sun Huiwei; Xu Zunming; Dong Zheng; Diao Chong; Lu Jingyu; Li Tonggui; Li Yexing

sentences.zh: 自晉永嘉之後，運鍾喪亂，宇內分崩，羣凶肆禍，生民不見俎豆之容，黔首唯覩戎馬之跡，禮樂文章，掃地將盡。

translations.literal: From after the Yongjia era of Jin, fortune struck calamity and disorder; within the four seas there was collapse; many villains unleashed disaster; the living people did not see the appearance of sacrificial vessels; the black-haired masses saw only the tracks of warhorses; rites, music, and literature were swept clean and nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia era of the Jin dynasty, the times were struck by calamity and disorder. The realm split apart, and villains ran riot. The common people no longer saw ritual vessels; they saw only the tracks of warhorses. Rites, music, and learning were all but swept away.

sentences.zh: 而契之所感，斯道猶存。

translations.literal: Yet what the covenant touched, this Way still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what fate had ordained still held, and the Way itself endured.

sentences.zh: 高才有德之流，自強蓬蓽；

translations.literal: The stream of men of lofty talent and virtue strengthened themselves from thatched huts;
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent and virtue strengthened themselves even in humble thatched cottages;

sentences.zh: 鴻生碩儒之輩，抱器晦己。

translations.literal: The class of great scholars and eminent Confucians held their talents and concealed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: while eminent scholars kept their learning close and lived in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 太祖初定中原，雖日不暇給，始建都邑，便以經術為先，立太學，置五經博士生員千有餘人。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor first settled the Central Plains, though his days allowed no respite, as soon as he established the capital he put classical learning first, founded the Imperial Academy, and appointed more than a thousand students for the Five Classics doctoral posts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder Emperor first secured the Central Plains, he had scarcely a moment to spare, yet as soon as he established his capital he made classical learning his first concern. He founded the Imperial Academy and enrolled more than a thousand students as doctoral candidates in the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 天興二年春，增國子太學生員至三千。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianxing, the number of Imperial Academy and National University students was increased to three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Tianxing, enrollment in the National University and Imperial Academy was raised to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 豈不以天下可馬上取之，不可以馬上治之，為國之道，文武兼用，毓才成務，意在茲乎？

translations.literal: Was it not because the realm may be taken on horseback but cannot be governed on horseback? The way to rule a state employs both civil and military arts together; nurturing talent to accomplish affairs—was not the intent in this?
translations.idiomatic: Did he not grasp that an empire may be won from horseback but cannot be ruled from horseback? To govern a state requires both civil and military means; to nurture talent and accomplish the work of government—was that not his purpose?

sentences.zh: 聖達經猷，蓋為遠矣。

translations.literal: The sagely penetration of the classics and plans—how far-reaching indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Such sage foresight in statecraft reached far indeed.

sentences.zh: 四年春，命樂師入學習舞，釋菜于先聖、先師。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year, he ordered music masters to enter the school to study the dances and performed the vegetable offering to the former Sage and former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he ordered music masters into the academy to learn the ritual dances and offered vegetables in sacrifice to the ancient Sage and Teacher.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，改國子為中書學，立教授博士。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong, the National University was changed to the Secretariat School, and instructing professors and doctors were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong the National University was renamed the Secretariat School, with professors and doctoral instructors appointed.

sentences.zh: 世祖始光三年春，別起太學於城東，後徵盧玄、高允等，而令州郡各舉才學。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Shiguang under Emperor Shizu, a separate Imperial Academy was built east of the city; later Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others were summoned, and the provinces and commanderies were each ordered to recommend men of learning and talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Shiguang under Emperor Shizu, a new Imperial Academy was built east of the city. Later he summoned Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others, and ordered each province and commandery to recommend men of learning and talent.

sentences.zh: 於是人多砥尚，儒林轉興。

translations.literal: Thereupon many people sharpened and esteemed learning, and the forest of scholars flourished anew.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter many took up the whetstone of learning, and the community of scholars flourished once more.

sentences.zh: 顯祖天安初，詔立鄉學，郡置博士二人，助教二人，學生六十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an under Emperor Xianzu, an edict established district schools: each commandery was to have two doctors, two assistant instructors, and sixty students.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tian'an era under Emperor Xianzu, an edict established district schools. Each commandery was to have two doctoral instructors, two assistant teachers, and sixty students.

sentences.zh: 後詔：大郡立博士二人，助教四人，學生一百人；

translations.literal: Later an edict stated: large commanderies were to have two doctors, four assistant instructors, and one hundred students;
translations.idiomatic: A later edict specified that large commanderies should have two doctors, four assistant instructors, and one hundred students;

sentences.zh: 次郡立博士二人，助教二人，學生八十人；

translations.literal: secondary commanderies two doctors, two assistant instructors, and eighty students;
translations.idiomatic: secondary commanderies two doctors, two assistants, and eighty students;

sentences.zh: 中郡立博士一人，助教二人，學生六十人；

translations.literal: middle commanderies one doctor, two assistant instructors, and sixty students;
translations.idiomatic: middle commanderies one doctor, two assistants, and sixty students;

sentences.zh: 下郡立博士一人，助教一人，學生四十人。

translations.literal: small commanderies one doctor, one assistant instructor, and forty students.
translations.idiomatic: and small commanderies one doctor, one assistant, and forty students.

sentences.zh: 太和中，改中書學為國子學，建明堂辟雍，尊三老五更，又開皇子之學。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, the Secretariat School was changed back to the National University; the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy precinct were built; the Three Elders and Five More-Honored were honored; and schooling for imperial princes was also opened.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era the Secretariat School was restored as the National University. The Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were built, the Three Elders and Five More-Honored were honored, and instruction was opened for the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 及遷都洛邑，詔立國子太學、四門小學。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, an edict established the National University, Imperial Academy, and Four Gates Elementary School.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved the capital to Luoyang, an edict founded the National University, the Imperial Academy, and the Four Gates Elementary School.

sentences.zh: 高祖欽明稽古，篤好墳典，坐輿據鞍，不忘講道。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was reverently clear in examining antiquity, deeply fond of the classics buried in tomes; seated in his carriage or mounted in the saddle, he never forgot to discuss the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was reverent toward antiquity and deeply devoted to the classics. Whether seated in his carriage or mounted on horseback, he never ceased lecturing on the Way.

sentences.zh: 劉芳、李彪諸人以經書進，崔光、邢巒之徒以文史達，其餘涉獵典章，關歷詞翰，莫不縻以好爵，動貽賞眷。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, Li Biao, and others advanced through the classics; Cui Guang, Xing Luan, and their kind achieved distinction through letters and histories; the rest who ranged through canonical regulations and passed through literary composition—all were tethered with fine ranks and constantly received favor and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, Li Biao, and others rose by presenting the classics; Cui Guang, Xing Luan, and their peers distinguished themselves in letters and history. All who ranged through the canon or excelled in literary composition were bound to fine offices and showered with favor.

sentences.zh: 於是斯文鬱然，比隆周漢。

translations.literal: Thereupon cultured writing flourished luxuriantly, rivaling the glory of Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thus learning flourished luxuriantly, rivaling the heights of the Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，復詔營國學，樹小學於四門，大選儒生，以為小學博士，員四十人。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizong, an edict again ordered construction of the National University and planting of an elementary school at the Four Gates; Confucian scholars were broadly selected to serve as elementary-school doctors, forty posts in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong an edict again ordered the National University rebuilt and an elementary school established at the Four Gates. Confucian scholars were chosen in large numbers as elementary-school doctors, forty in all.

sentences.zh: 雖黌宇未立，而經術彌顯。

translations.literal: Although the school buildings were not yet completed, classical learning grew ever more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Though the school buildings were not yet finished, classical learning shone all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，學業大盛。

translations.literal: At the time the realm enjoyed peace, and scholarly pursuit greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace, and learning flourished on every side.

sentences.zh: 故燕齊趙魏之間，橫經著錄，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Thus between Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei, those who stretched the classics and were entered in registers were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei, students seated with classics before them and names entered in school registers were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 大者千餘人，小者猶數百。

translations.literal: The large had more than a thousand men; the small still had several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The largest schools had more than a thousand pupils; even the smallest still had several hundred.

sentences.zh: 州舉茂異，郡貢孝廉，對揚王庭，每年逾眾。

translations.literal: Provinces recommended outstanding men; commanderies presented Filial and Incorrupt candidates; they answered and exalted at the royal court, and each year the numbers exceeded the last.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces recommended outstanding scholars, commanderies sent up Filial and Incorrupt candidates, and each year more and more appeared at court to expound their learning before the throne.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，將立國學，詔以三品已上及五品清官之子以充生選。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era, when the National University was about to be established, an edict ordered sons of officials of the third rank and above and of fifth-rank pure offices to fill the student selections.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era, as the National University was about to be founded, an edict specified that sons of officials of the third rank and above, and of fifth-rank pure offices, should fill the student places.

sentences.zh: 未及簡置，仍復停寢。

translations.literal: Before selection and appointment could be completed, the plan was again suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Before the selections could be made, the project was suspended once again.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，乃釋奠於國學，命祭酒崔光講孝經，始置國子生三十六人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang, the vegetable offering was finally performed at the National University; the Rector Cui Guang was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and thirty-six National University students were first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang the court at last performed the sacrifice at the National University, ordered Rector Cui Guang to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and enrolled the first thirty-six National University students.

sentences.zh: 暨孝昌之後，海內淆亂，四方校學所存無幾。

translations.literal: After the Xiaochang era, within the seas there was turmoil; of the schools in the four directions scarcely any remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiaochang era the realm fell into chaos, and few schools survived anywhere in the land.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，復釋奠於國學；

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, the vegetable offering was again performed at the National University;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era the sacrifice was again performed at the National University;

sentences.zh: 又於顯陽殿詔祭酒劉廞講孝經，黃門李郁說禮記，中書舍人盧景宣講大戴禮夏小正篇；

translations.literal: also at the Xianyang Hall an edict had Rector Liu Yin lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen Li Yu expound the Record of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan lecture on the Xiaozheng chapter of the Elder Dai's Record of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: and at the Xianyang Hall the court ordered Rector Liu Yin to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen Li Yu to expound the Record of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan to lecture on the Xiaozheng chapter of the Elder Dai's Record of Rites;

sentences.zh: 復置生七十二人。

translations.literal: seventy-two students were again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: and enrolled seventy-two students anew.

sentences.zh: 及遷都於鄴，國子置生三十六人。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Ye, the National University appointed thirty-six students.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved the capital to Ye, the National University enrolled thirty-six students.

sentences.zh: 至於興和、武定之世，寇難既平，儒業復光矣。

translations.literal: By the eras of Xinghe and Wuding, once bandit troubles had been pacified, Confucian pursuit shone again.
translations.idiomatic: By the eras of Xinghe and Wuding, once the invasions had been quelled, Confucian learning shone forth again.

sentences.zh: 漢世鄭玄並為眾經注解，服虔、何休各有所說。

translations.literal: In Han times Zheng Xuan annotated all the classics; Fu Qian and He Xiu each had their own explanations.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Zheng Xuan annotated the classics, while Fu Qian and He Xiu each had their own schools of interpretation.

sentences.zh: 玄易、書、詩、禮、論語、孝經，虔左氏春秋，休公羊傳，大行於河北。

translations.literal: Xuan's commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, Fu Qian's Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn, and He Xiu's Gongyang Commentary greatly prevailed in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, Fu Qian's Zuo Commentary, and He Xiu's Gongyang Commentary all flourished in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 王肅易亦間行焉。

translations.literal: Wang Su's commentary on the Changes also circulated there from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's commentary on the Changes also circulated there at times.

sentences.zh: 晉世杜預注左氏，預玄孫坦、坦弟驥於劉義隆世並為青州刺史，傳其家業，故齊地多習之。

translations.literal: In Jin times Du Yu annotated the Zuo Commentary; Yu's great-great-grandson Tan and Tan's younger brother Ji, both in the era of Liu Yilong, served as governors of Qing Province and transmitted the family learning, so the Qi region largely studied it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times Du Yu annotated the Zuo Commentary. His great-great-grandsons Tan and Ji both served as governors of Qing Province under Liu Yilong and transmitted the family tradition, so the Qi region largely followed Du Yu's school.

sentences.zh: 自梁越以下傳受講說者甚眾。

translations.literal: From Liang Yue downward, those who transmitted and received instruction in lecturing were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang Yue onward, very many transmitted and taught these traditions.

sentences.zh: 今舉其知名者附列於後云。

translations.literal: Now their well-known names are gathered and appended below.
translations.idiomatic: Here we list the best known of them in what follows.

sentences.zh: 梁越，字玄覽，新興人也。

translations.literal: Liang Yue, courtesy name Xuanlan, was a native of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yue, whose courtesy name was Xuanlan, came from Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 少而好學，博綜經傳，無所不通。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, broadly mastered the classics and their traditions, and had nothing he did not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and mastered the classics and their commentaries so thoroughly that nothing in them was closed to him.

sentences.zh: 性純和篤信，行無擇善。

translations.literal: His nature was pure, harmonious, and deeply faithful; in conduct he never chose between good acts.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was pure, gentle, and deeply sincere; in every action he did what was right without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 國初為禮經博士。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he served as doctor of the Rites Classic.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he served as doctoral instructor in the Rites Classic.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其謹厚，舉動可則，拜上大夫，命授諸皇子經書。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor, because of his prudence and solidity and because his conduct could serve as a model, appointed him Senior Grand Master and ordered him to teach the classics to the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder Emperor, finding him prudent and steadfast and his conduct worthy of imitation, appointed him Senior Grand Master and charged him with instructing the imperial princes in the classics.

sentences.zh: 太宗即祚，以師傅之恩賜爵祝阿侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, in gratitude for his service as tutor he was granted the title Marquis of Zhu'e.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he rewarded Yue's service as tutor with the title Marquis of Zhu'e.

sentences.zh: 後出為雁門太守，獲白雀以獻，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he went out as governor of Yanmen, obtained a white sparrow and presented it, and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Yanmen, where he captured a white sparrow and presented it to the throne; he was then appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子弼，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Bi died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi died young.

sentences.zh: 弼子恭，襲。

translations.literal: Bi's son Gong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's son Gong inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 降為雲中子。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Viscount of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The title was later reduced to Viscount of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son, and the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 盧醜，昌黎徒河人，襄城王魯元之族也。

translations.literal: Lu Chou, a native of Tuhe in Changli, was of the same clan as Prince of Xiangcheng Lu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chou came from Tuhe in Changli and was a kinsman of Prince of Xiangcheng Lu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 世祖之為監國，醜以篤學博聞入授世祖經。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu was Heir Apparent, Chou entered to teach the Heir the classics on account of his solid learning and broad knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu was crown prince, Chou was summoned to instruct him in the classics on account of his solid learning and wide knowledge.

sentences.zh: 後以師傅舊恩賜爵濟陰公。

translations.literal: Later, in recognition of his former favor as tutor, he was granted the title Duke of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in gratitude for his service as tutor, the court granted him the title Duke of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 除鎮軍將軍，拜尚書，加散騎常侍，出為河內太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, made Minister, given the additional title of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and went out as governor of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, made a minister of state, given the additional title of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and later served as governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 延和二年冬卒。

translations.literal: He died in winter of the second year of Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the second year of Yanhe.

translations.literal: 〈Missing〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Missing text〉

sentences.zh: 初，中山襲爵，太和中，以老疾自免。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongshan inherited the title; in the Taihe era, on account of age and illness he excused himself from office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhongshan had inherited the title; during the Taihe era he retired on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 子升頭，襲爵，後例降。

translations.literal: His son Sheng'tou inherited the title and later, by precedent, was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng'tou inherited the title and was later demoted by the usual precedent.

sentences.zh: 張偉，字仲業，小名翠螭，太原中都人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, courtesy name Zhongye, childhood name Cuichi, was a native of Zhongdu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, whose courtesy name was Zhongye and childhood name Cuichi, came from Zhongdu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖敏，晉祕書監。

translations.literal: His ancestor Min was Director of the Secretariat under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Min had served as Director of the Secretariat under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 偉學通諸經，講授鄉里，受業者常數百人。

translations.literal: Wei mastered all the classics in learning, lectured in his home district, and those who received his instruction were often several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wei mastered all the classics and taught in his home district, where his students often numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 儒謹汎納，勤於教訓，雖有頑固不曉，問至數十，偉告喻殷勤，曾無慍色。

translations.literal: Confucian, prudent, broadly accepting, diligent in instruction and admonition—even when there were the stubborn who did not understand, though questioned dozens of times, Wei explained and instructed with earnest care and never once showed anger.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian in bearing, prudent and open-handed, he was tireless in teaching. Even when dull students failed to understand and questioned him dozens of times, he explained with patient care and never showed irritation.

sentences.zh: 常依附經典，教以孝悌，門人感其仁化，事之如父。

translations.literal: He always relied on the classics, teaching filial piety and brotherly duty; his disciples, moved by his humane transforming influence, served him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: He always grounded his teaching in the classics, instructing his pupils in filial piety and brotherly duty. Moved by his humane influence, they treated him as a father.

sentences.zh: 性恬平，不以夷嶮易操，清雅篤慎，非法不言。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil and even; he did not alter his conduct for ease or peril; refined, pure, deeply prudent—what was not lawful he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was calm and even; he did not change his conduct for ease or danger. Refined and deeply prudent, he would speak only what was lawful.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，與高允等俱被辟命，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizu's time, together with Gao Yun and others he was summoned by appointment and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu he was summoned to court with Gao Yun and others and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉侍郎、大將軍樂安王範從事中郎、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant Gentleman to General-in-Chief Prince of Le'an Fan, and governor of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then served as Attendant Gentleman to General-in-Chief Prince Fan of Le'an, and later as governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 還，仍為中書侍郎、本國大中正。

translations.literal: On his return he again served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and Grand Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he again served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and as Grand Rectifier of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 使酒泉，慰勞沮渠無諱。

translations.literal: He was sent to Jiuquan to console and comfort Juqu Wuhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to Jiuquan to console Juqu Wuhui.

sentences.zh: 還，遷散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 聘劉義隆還，拜給事中、建威將軍，賜爵成臯子。

translations.literal: After an embassy to Liu Yilong he returned and was appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Establishes Might, and was granted the title Viscount of Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from an embassy to Liu Yilong, he was appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Establishes Might and granted the title Viscount of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 出為平東將軍、營州刺史，進爵建安公。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Ying Province, and was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Ying Province, and was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征南將軍、并州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given General Who Conquers the South and governor of Bing Province; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the South and governor of Bing Province, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 在州郡以仁德為先，不任刑罰，清身率下，宰守不敢為非。

translations.literal: In provinces and commanderies he put humaneness and virtue first, did not rely on punishments, kept his person pure and led those below; magistrates and governors did not dare do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial office he put benevolence first and did not rely on punishments. By keeping himself pure he led his subordinates, and local officials did not dare misconduct themselves.

sentences.zh: 子仲慮，太和初，假給事中、高麗副使，尋假散騎常侍、高麗使。

translations.literal: His son Zhonglü, at the beginning of Taihe, was provisionally made Palace Attendant and deputy envoy to Goguryeo; soon after he was provisionally made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhonglü, at the opening of the Taihe era, served provisionally as Palace Attendant and deputy envoy to Goguryeo, and soon after as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 後出為章武太守，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: Later he went out as governor of Zhangwu and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Zhangwu with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 仲慮弟仲繼，學尚有父風，善倉、雅、林說。

translations.literal: Zhonglü's younger brother Zhongji, in learning still had his father's manner; he was skilled in the explanations of Cang, Ya, and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü's younger brother Zhongji inherited his father's scholarly manner and was skilled in the glossaries known as Cang, Ya, and Lin.

sentences.zh: 太和中，官至侍御長，坐事徙西裔，道死。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he reached the post of Chief of Palace Attendants; because of an offense he was banished to the western frontier and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he rose to Chief of Palace Attendants, but was banished to the western frontier for an offense and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 梁祚，北地泥陽人。

translations.literal: Liang Zuo was a native of Niyang in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zuo came from Niyang in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 父劭，皇始二年歸國，拜吏部郎，出為濟陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Shao, in the second year of Huangshi, submitted to the state and was appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, then went out as governor of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao submitted to the Wei state in the second year of Huangshi, was appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, and later served as governor of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 至祚居趙郡。

translations.literal: By the time of Zuo the family resided in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By Zuo's time the family had settled in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祚篤志好學，歷治諸經，尤善公羊春秋、鄭氏易，常以教授。

translations.literal: Zuo had a steadfast will and loved learning; he studied all the classics in turn and was especially skilled in the Gongyang Commentary to the Spring and Autumn and Zheng Xuan's Changes, which he constantly used in teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was devoted to learning and studied all the classics in turn. He was especially skilled in the Gongyang Commentary and Zheng Xuan's Changes, which he taught throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 有儒者風，而無當世之才。

translations.literal: He had the air of a Confucian scholar but lacked talent for his own age.
translations.idiomatic: He had the bearing of a Confucian scholar but lacked the talent to make his mark in public life.

sentences.zh: 與幽州別駕平恒有舊，又姊先適范陽李氏，遂攜家人僑居於薊。

translations.literal: He had an old friendship with Ping Heng, Administrator of You Province; moreover his elder sister had earlier married into the Li clan of Fanyang, so he took his family and sojourned in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was an old friend of Ping Heng, Administrator of You Province, and his elder sister had earlier married into the Li family of Fanyang. He therefore moved his household to Ji as sojourners.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，雖覊旅貧窘而著述不倦。

translations.literal: For more than ten years, though a traveler in straits and poor, he never wearied of writing.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years, though living abroad in poverty, he never wearied of writing.

sentences.zh: 恒時相請屈，與論經史。

translations.literal: Heng often invited him to stay and discussed the classics and histories with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Heng often invited him to stay and discuss the classics and histories with him.

sentences.zh: 辟祕書中散，稍遷祕書令。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Attendant and gradually promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Secretariat Attendant and gradually rose to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為李訢所排，擯退為中書博士。

translations.literal: He was pushed aside by Li Xin and demoted to Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin forced him aside and he was demoted to Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後出為統萬鎮司馬，徵為散令。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Administrator of Tongwan Garrison and was recalled as Scattered Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Administrator of Tongwan Garrison and was recalled as Scattered Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 撰并陳壽三國志，名曰國統。

translations.literal: He compiled and merged Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, entitling it National Succession.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a merged edition of Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms under the title National Succession.

sentences.zh: 又作代都賦，頗行於世。

translations.literal: He also composed a Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai, which circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 清貧守素，不交勢貴。

translations.literal: Pure and poor, he kept to simplicity and did not associate with the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but upright, he kept to simplicity and would not court the powerful.

sentences.zh: 年八十七，太和十二年卒。

translations.literal: At the age of eighty-seven he died in the twelfth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Taihe at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子元吉，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Yuanji had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanji inherited his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 少子重，歷碎職，後為相州鎮北府參軍事。

translations.literal: His youngest son Chong passed through minor posts and later served as Staff Officer of the Northern Garrison Headquarters of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Chong served in minor posts and later became Staff Officer of the Northern Garrison Headquarters of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 平恒，字繼叔，燕國薊人。

translations.literal: Ping Heng, courtesy name Jishu, was a native of Ji in Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Heng, whose courtesy name was Jishu, came from Ji in Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖視，父儒，並仕慕容為通宦。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi and his father Ru both served the Murong as general clerical officials.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi and his father Ru had both served the Murong as general-purpose court officials.

sentences.zh: 恒耽勤讀誦，研綜經籍，鉤深致遠，多所博聞。

translations.literal: Heng devoted himself diligently to reading and recitation, investigated and synthesized the classics, probed deep and reached far, and was widely learned.
translations.idiomatic: Heng applied himself tirelessly to reading and recitation, mastered the classics through deep and far-reaching study, and became a man of broad learning.

sentences.zh: 自周以降，暨於魏世，帝王傳代之由，貴臣昇降之緒，皆撰錄品第，商略是非，號曰略注，合百餘篇。

translations.literal: From the Zhou dynasty downward through the Wei age, he compiled and ranked the reasons for the succession of emperors and kings and the threads of the rise and fall of eminent ministers, weighed right and wrong, and called the work Brief Notes, more than a hundred chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou dynasty down through the Wei, he compiled and ranked the reasons dynasties rose and fell and the careers of great ministers rose and declined, judged their merits and faults, and called the work Brief Notes—more than a hundred chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 好事者覽之，咸以為善焉。

translations.literal: Those who delighted in such things, on reading it, all regarded it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Readers who took an interest in such matters all agreed that it was excellent.

sentences.zh: 安貧樂道，不以屢空改操。

translations.literal: He was content in poverty and devoted to the Way, and did not change his conduct because his household was repeatedly empty.
translations.idiomatic: He was content with poverty and devoted to the Way, and never altered his principles even when his household was repeatedly destitute.

sentences.zh: 徵為中書博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為幽州別駕。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was sent out as Administrator of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted out of the capital as Administrator of You Province.

sentences.zh: 廉貞寡欲，不營資產，衣食至常不足，妻子不免飢寒。

translations.literal: Incorruptible and upright, with few desires, he did not pursue property; his food and clothing were often insufficient, and his wife and children could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Incorruptible and abstemious, he made no effort to build up his estate; food and clothing were often scarce, and his wife and children still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 後拜著作佐郎，遷祕書丞。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Editing Assistant, then promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Editing Assistant and then promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時高允為監，河間邢祐、[2]北平陽嘏、河東裴定、廣平程駿、金城趙元順等為著作佐郎，雖才學互有短長，然俱為稱職，並號長者。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Yun served as Supervisor; Xing You of Hejian, Yang Gu of Beiping, Pei Ding of Hedong, Cheng Jun of Guangping, Zhao Yuanshun of Jincheng, and others served as Editing Assistants. Though their talent and learning each had strengths and weaknesses, all performed their duties well and were alike called men of stature.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Yun was Supervisor, while Xing You of Hejian, Yang Gu of Beiping, Pei Ding of Hedong, Cheng Jun of Guangping, Zhao Yuanshun of Jincheng, and others served as Editing Assistants. Their talents varied, yet all were regarded as competent and were known as men of standing.

sentences.zh: 允每稱博通經籍無過恒也。

translations.literal: Gao Yun always said that in comprehensive mastery of the classics none surpassed Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun always maintained that no one surpassed Heng in thorough mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 恒即劉彧將軍王玄謨舅子。

translations.literal: Heng was the nephew by marriage of General Wang Xuamo of Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was a nephew by marriage of Liu Yu's general Wang Xuamo.

sentences.zh: 恒三子，並不率父業，好酒自棄。

translations.literal: Heng's three sons all failed to follow their father's profession and, loving wine, ruined themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's three sons all abandoned their father's path and, given to drink, wasted themselves.

sentences.zh: 恒常忿其世衰，植杖巡舍側崗而哭，不為營事婚宦，任意官娶，故仕聘濁碎，不得及其門流。

translations.literal: Heng often resented that their generation had declined; leaning on his staff he would walk along the ridge beside his house and weep. He did not arrange marriages for them and let them marry as officials saw fit, so official matches became muddied and inferior, and none could match the standing of his house.
translations.idiomatic: Heng often grieved that his sons' generation had fallen away; leaning on his staff he would walk the ridge beside his home and weep. He would not arrange their marriages and let them marry as officials saw fit, so their official matches grew coarse and unworthy, and none could uphold the family's standing.

sentences.zh: 恒婦弟鄧宗慶及外生孫玄明等每以為言。

translations.literal: Heng's wife's younger brother Deng Zongqing and his sister's son Sun Xuanming and others often spoke to him about this.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's brother-in-law Deng Zongqing, his sister's son Sun Xuanming, and others often remonstrated with him about it.

sentences.zh: 恒曰：「此輩會是衰頓，何煩勞我。

translations.literal: Heng said, "This lot are bound to decline and fail—why should they trouble me?"
translations.idiomatic: Heng said, "That bunch are sure to sink into ruin—why should I bother with them?"

sentences.zh: 」乃別構精廬，并置經籍於其中，一奴自給，妻子莫得而往，酒食亦不與同。

translations.literal: He then built a separate refined dwelling and placed his classics within it; one servant supplied his needs, his wife and children were not allowed to go there, and he did not share food or drink with them.
translations.idiomatic: So he built a separate refined retreat and kept his classics there; a single servant attended him, his wife and children were forbidden to visit, and he no longer shared meals with them.

sentences.zh: 時有珍美，呼時老東安公刁雍等共飲噉之，家人無得嘗焉。

translations.literal: When there were fine delicacies, he would summon the venerable Duke of Dong'an, Diao Yong, and others to eat and drink with him; his family was not allowed to taste them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there were choice delicacies, he would call the venerable Duke of Dong'an, Diao Yong, and others to share the feast; his family was never allowed a taste.

sentences.zh: 太和十年，以恒為祕書令，而恒固請為郡，未授而卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taihe he was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat, but Heng firmly requested a post in the provinces; before the appointment was granted he died, at the age of seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Taihe he was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat, but Heng insisted on taking a provincial post; before the appointment could be made he died, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、幽州刺史、都昌侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the title General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of You Province, and Marquis of Duchang; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of You Province, and Marquis of Duchang, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 子壽昌，太和初，祕書令史。

translations.literal: His son Shouchang, in the early Taihe era, served as Clerk to the Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouchang served in the early Taihe era as Clerk to the Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 稍遷荊州征虜府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Recording Secretary in the General Who Conquers Barbarians Headquarters of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Recording Secretary in the Jing Province headquarters of the General Who Conquers Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 陳奇，字脩奇，河北人也，自云晉涼州刺史驤之八世孫。

translations.literal: Chen Qi, courtesy name Xiuqi, was a man of Hebei and claimed to be the eighth-generation descendant of Xiang, Governor of Liang Province under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qi, whose courtesy name was Xiuqi, came from Hebei and claimed descent from Xiang, Governor of Liang Province under the Jin, eight generations back.

sentences.zh: 祖刃，仕慕容垂。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ren served Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ren had served Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 奇少孤，家貧，而奉母至孝。

translations.literal: Qi lost his father while young; though his family was poor, he served his mother with the utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was orphaned young; his family was poor, yet he served his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 齠齓聰識，有夙成之美。

translations.literal: Even in childhood he was clever and perceptive, and possessed the excellence of early maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was bright and perceptive, showing the promise of precocious talent.

sentences.zh: 性氣剛亮，與俗不羣。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and upright, and he did not flock with the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature forceful and upright, and kept apart from ordinary company.

sentences.zh: 愛玩經典，博通墳籍，常非馬融、鄭玄解經失旨，志在著述五經。

translations.literal: He loved and studied the classics, was broadly versed in ancient texts, often criticized Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan for missing the true intent in their commentaries, and aspired to compose works on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics and mastered the ancient texts, often faulting Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan for misreading the true intent of the scriptures, and set his heart on writing commentaries on the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 始注孝經、論語，頗傳於世，為搢紳所稱。

translations.literal: He first annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, which circulated widely in the world and were praised by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: He began with commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, which gained wide circulation and won praise from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 與河間邢祐同召赴京。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital together with Xing You of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital together with Xing You of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 時祕書監游雅素聞其名，始頗好之，引入祕省，欲授以史職。

translations.literal: At that time You Ya, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, had long heard his reputation, at first favored him greatly, brought him into the secretariat, and wished to assign him to historical duties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time You Ya, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, had long known his reputation; he initially took a strong liking to him, brought him into the secretariat, and intended to give him a post in historiography.

sentences.zh: 後與奇論典誥及詩書，雅贊扶馬鄭。

translations.literal: Later, when he discussed the Canon of Documents and the Classic of Poetry with Qi, Ya praised and upheld Ma and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he discussed the Canon of Documents and the Classic of Poetry with Qi, Ya spoke in praise of Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 至於易訟卦天與水違行，雅曰：「自葱嶺以西，水皆西流，推此而言，易之所及自葱嶺以東耳。

translations.literal: When the discussion turned to the Song hexagram in the Changes—"Heaven and water move contrary"—Ya said, "West of the Congling Mountains all rivers flow westward; by that reasoning, the reach of the Changes extends only east of the Congling Mountains."
translations.idiomatic: When they came to the Song hexagram in the Book of Changes—"Heaven and water move contrary to each other"—Ya said, "West of the Congling Mountains all waters flow westward; if we follow that logic, the Book of Changes applies only to lands east of the Congling Mountains."

sentences.zh: 」奇曰：「易理綿廣，包含宇宙。

translations.literal: Qi said, "The principles of the Changes are vast and broad and embrace the cosmos."
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "The principles of the Changes are vast and broad; they encompass the whole cosmos."

sentences.zh: 若如公言，自葱嶺以西，豈東向望天哉？

translations.literal: "If it were as you say, west of the Congling Mountains would people not look eastward to see Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: "If what you say were true, west of the Congling Mountains would people not still look eastward to behold Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」奇執義非雅，每如此類，終不苟從。

translations.literal: Qi held to principle and opposed Ya; in matters like this he never casually followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi stood by his own reading and opposed Ya; on points like these he never simply yielded.

sentences.zh: 雅性護短，因以為嫌。

translations.literal: Ya was by nature protective of his own faults, and on this account came to bear a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was by nature quick to shield his own shortcomings, and from this he came to resent Qi.

sentences.zh: 嘗眾辱奇，或爾汝之，或指為小人。

translations.literal: He once humiliated Qi before a crowd, sometimes addressing him with the familiar pronouns er and ru, sometimes calling him a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he publicly humiliated Qi, sometimes addressing him with familiar pronouns and sometimes calling him a petty man.

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「公身為君子，奇身且小人耳。

translations.literal: Qi said, "Your lordship is a gentleman; I am only a petty man."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Your lordship is a gentleman; I am but a petty man."

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「君言身且小人，君祖父是何人也？

translations.literal: Ya said, "You say you are a petty man—what sort of man was your grandfather?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, "You call yourself a petty man—then what sort of man was your grandfather?"

sentences.zh: 」奇曰：「祖，燕東部侯釐。

translations.literal: Qi said, "My grandfather was Chi, Eastern Marquis of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "My grandfather was Chi, Eastern Marquis of Yan."

sentences.zh: 」[3]雅質奇曰：「侯釐何官也？

translations.literal: Ya pressed Qi and said, "What office was Marquis Chi?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya pressed him: "What office was Marquis Chi?"

sentences.zh: 」奇曰：「三皇不傳禮，官名豈同哉？

translations.literal: Qi said, "The Three Sovereigns did not transmit the rites—how could office titles be the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "The Three Sovereigns did not hand down the rites—how could official titles remain the same?"

sentences.zh: 故昔有雲師、火正、鳥師之名。

translations.literal: "Hence in antiquity there were such names as Cloud Master, Fire Rectifier, and Bird Master."
translations.idiomatic: "That is why antiquity knew such titles as Cloud Master, Fire Rectifier, and Bird Master."

sentences.zh: 以斯而言，世革則官異，時易則禮變。

translations.literal: "From this it follows that when the age changes, offices differ, and when the times shift, rites change."
translations.idiomatic: "From this it follows that when the age changes offices differ, and when the times turn rites change as well."

sentences.zh: 公為皇魏東宮內侍長，侍長竟何職也？

translations.literal: "Your lordship is Attendant Chief of the Eastern Palace of Great Wei—what office is Attendant Chief after all?"
translations.idiomatic: "Your lordship served as Attendant Chief of the Eastern Palace under Great Wei—what office, after all, is Attendant Chief?"

sentences.zh: 」由是雅深憾之。

translations.literal: From this Ya deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Ya came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 先是敕以奇付雅，令銓補祕書，雅既惡之，遂不復敍用焉。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had assigned Qi to Ya's charge with orders to assess and appoint him in the secretariat, but Ya, having come to detest him, never employed him.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had placed Qi under Ya's supervision for appointment in the secretariat, but Ya, who now despised him, never gave him a post.

sentences.zh: 奇冗散數年，高允與奇讎溫古籍，嘉其遠致，稱奇通識，非凡學所窺。

translations.literal: Qi remained idle and unsalaried for several years; Gao Yun collated ancient texts with him, admired his far-reaching insight, and said that Qi's comprehensive knowledge was beyond what ordinary scholarship could fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Qi remained idle and without appointment for several years. Gao Yun worked with him collating ancient texts, admired his far-reaching insight, and declared that Qi's comprehensive learning lay beyond ordinary scholarship.

sentences.zh: 允微勸雅曰：「君朝望具瞻，何為與野儒辨簡牘章句？

translations.literal: Gao Yun subtly urged Ya, saying, "Your standing in court is widely watched—why debate bamboo-slip clauses with rustic scholars?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun gently urged Ya, saying, "Your standing at court is widely watched—why wrangle over textual minutiae with rustic scholars?"

sentences.zh: 」雅謂允有私於奇，曰：「君寧黨小人也！

translations.literal: Ya thought Gao Yun was privately partial to Qi and said, "Would you really side with a petty man!"
translations.idiomatic: Ya assumed Gao Yun was privately favoring Qi and said, "So you would actually take the side of a petty man!"

sentences.zh: 」乃取奇所注論語、孝經焚於坑內。

translations.literal: He then took Qi's annotated Analects and Classic of Filial Piety and burned them in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Qi's commentaries on the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety and burned them in a pit.

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「公貴人，不乏樵薪，何乃燃奇論語？

translations.literal: Qi said, "Your lordship is a noble and lacks no firewood—why burn Qi's Analects?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Your lordship is a man of rank and cannot lack firewood—why burn Qi's Analects?"

sentences.zh: 」雅愈怒，因告京師後生不聽傳授。

translations.literal: Ya grew still angrier and therefore forbade the younger scholars of the capital to transmit or teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Ya grew still angrier and forbade the younger scholars of the capital to transmit or teach Qi's works.

sentences.zh: 而奇無降志，亦評雅之失。

translations.literal: Yet Qi did not lower his resolve and also criticized Ya's errors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi did not soften his stance and continued to criticize Ya's mistakes.

sentences.zh: 雅製昭皇太后碑文，論后名字之美，比諭前魏之甄后。

translations.literal: Ya composed an epitaph for Empress Dowager Zhao, discussing the beauty of the empress's name and comparing her to Empress Zhen of Former Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ya composed an epitaph for Empress Dowager Zhao, praising the beauty of the empress's name and drawing a comparison with Empress Zhen of Former Wei.

sentences.zh: 奇刺發其非，遂聞於上。

translations.literal: Qi exposed the error, and the matter reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Qi exposed the mistake, and word of it reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔下司徒檢對碑史事，乃郭后，雅有屈焉。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering the Minister of Education to verify the historical matters in the epitaph; it turned out to concern Empress Guo, and Ya was put in the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Minister of Education to verify the historical facts in the epitaph; the empress in question proved to be Empress Guo, and Ya was shown to be in error.

sentences.zh: 有人為謗書，多怨時之言，頗稱奇不得志。

translations.literal: Someone wrote a seditious book containing many complaints against the times, and it spoke rather favorably of Qi's frustrated ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Someone circulated a seditious tract full of grievances against the age, and it spoke with some sympathy of Qi's thwarted ambitions.

sentences.zh: 雅乃諷在事云：「此書言奇不遂，當是奇假人為之。

translations.literal: Ya then hinted to those in office, saying, "This book says Qi did not succeed—it must have been written by Qi through someone else."
translations.idiomatic: Ya then hinted to officials in charge, saying, "This book says Qi did not succeed in life—it must have been written by Qi through an accomplice."

sentences.zh: 如依律文，造謗書者皆及孥戮。

translations.literal: "According to the statutes, all who compose seditious books are subject to execution extending to their families."
translations.idiomatic: "Under the law, anyone who composes a seditious book is liable to execution extending to his whole family."

sentences.zh: 」遂抵奇罪。

translations.literal: Qi was therefore charged with the crime.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis Qi was charged with the crime.

sentences.zh: 時司徒、平原王陸麗知奇見枉，惜其才學，故得遷延經年，冀有寬宥。

translations.literal: At that time the Minister of Education, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li, knew Qi had been wronged and valued his talent and learning, so the case was delayed for years in the hope of clemency.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Minister of Education, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li, knew Qi had been wronged and valued his learning, so the case was delayed for years in the hope of mercy.

sentences.zh: 但執以獄成，竟致大戮，遂及其家。

translations.literal: But the prosecutors insisted the case was complete, and in the end he suffered capital punishment, which extended to his family as well.
translations.idiomatic: But the prosecutors insisted the case was closed, and in the end he was executed, and punishment extended to his family as well.

sentences.zh: 奇於易尤長，在獄嘗自筮卦，未及成，乃擥破而歎曰：「吾不度來年冬季！

translations.literal: Qi was especially accomplished in the Changes; while in prison he once divined for himself, and before the divination was complete he tore it apart and sighed, "I do not expect to survive until next winter!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi was especially skilled in the Book of Changes; while in prison he once cast a divination for himself, and before it was finished he tore the lines apart and sighed, "I do not expect to live through next winter!"

sentences.zh: 」及奇受害，如其所占。

translations.literal: When Qi met with disaster, it happened just as he had divined.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi met his death, events unfolded exactly as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 奇初被召，夜夢星墜壓脚，明而告人曰：「星則好風，星則好雨，夢星壓脚，必無善徵。

translations.literal: When Qi was first summoned, he dreamed at night that a star fell and crushed his foot; at dawn he told others, "Stars favor wind, stars favor rain—a dream of a star crushing the foot can surely be no good omen."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was first summoned, he dreamed that a star fell and crushed his foot; the next morning he told others, "Stars bring wind, stars bring rain—a dream of a star crushing one's foot can hardly be a good sign."

sentences.zh: 但時命峻切，不敢不赴耳。

translations.literal: "But the summons of the age was urgent, and I dared not fail to go."
translations.idiomatic: "But the summons was urgent, and I dared not refuse to go."

sentences.zh: 」奇妹適常氏，有子曰矯之，仕歷郡守。

translations.literal: Qi's younger sister married into the Chang clan and had a son named Jiaozhi, who served in succession as prefect of various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's younger sister married into the Chang clan and bore a son named Jiaozhi, who served in turn as prefect of several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，上書陳時政所宜，言頗忠至，清河王懌稱美之。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he submitted a memorial setting forth what was fitting in current policy; his words were quite loyal and sincere, and Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi praised them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era he submitted a memorial on what current policy ought to be; his words were notably loyal and forthright, and Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi praised them.

sentences.zh: 奇所注論語，矯之傳掌，未能行於世，其義多異鄭玄，往往與司徒崔浩同。

translations.literal: The Analects annotated by Qi was transmitted and preserved by Jiaozhi, but could not circulate in the world; its interpretations often differed from Zheng Xuan and frequently agreed with the Minister of Education Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's commentary on the Analects was handed down by Jiaozhi but never gained wide circulation; its readings often diverged from Zheng Xuan and frequently agreed with those of the Minister of Education Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 常爽，字仕明，河內溫人，魏太常卿林六世孫也。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang, courtesy name Shiming, was a native of Wen in Henei and the sixth-generation descendant of Lin, Grand Master of Ceremonies under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang, whose courtesy name was Shiming, came from Wen in Henei and was the sixth-generation descendant of Lin, Grand Master of Ceremonies under Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖珍，苻堅南安太守，因世亂遂居涼州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Nan'an under Fu Jian and, because of the turmoil of the age, settled in Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had been Administrator of Nan'an under Fu Jian; amid the chaos of the times he settled in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 父坦，乞伏世鎮遠將軍、大夏鎮將、顯美侯。

translations.literal: His father Tan, under the Qifu regime, was General Who Pacifies the Distance, Garrison Commander of Daxia, and Marquis of Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan, under the Qifu regime, held the titles General Who Pacifies the Distance, Garrison Commander of Daxia, and Marquis of Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 爽少而聰敏，嚴正有志概，雖家人僮隸未嘗見其寬誕之容。

translations.literal: Shuang was clever from youth, strict and upright with lofty resolve; even family members and servants never saw a relaxed or playful expression on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was clever from childhood, stern and upright with a strong sense of purpose; even family and servants never saw him wear a lax or playful look.

sentences.zh: 篤志好學，博聞強識，明習緯候，五經百家多所研綜。

translations.literal: He was devoted in purpose and loved learning, broadly informed and strongly retentive, clearly versed in apocryphal texts and astronomical portents, and extensively investigated and synthesized the Five Classics and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply committed to learning, possessed broad knowledge and a strong memory, was well versed in apocryphal texts and celestial portents, and had extensively mastered the Five Classics and the hundred schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮命皆不就。

translations.literal: He declined all honorable summons from provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every honorable summons issued by provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 世祖西征涼土，爽與兄仕國歸款軍門，世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu marched west against Liang, Shuang and his elder brother Shiguo surrendered at the army gates, and Emperor Shizu commended them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched west against Liang, Shuang and his elder brother Shiguo came over to the army and surrendered; Emperor Shizu praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 賜仕國爵五品，顯美男；

translations.literal: Shiguo was granted a fifth-rank noble title and made Baron of Xianmei;
translations.idiomatic: Shiguo was granted a fifth-rank noble title and made Baron of Xianmei;

sentences.zh: 爽為六品，拜宣威將軍。

translations.literal: Shuang received the sixth rank and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang received the sixth rank and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might.

sentences.zh: 是時戎車屢駕，征伐為事，貴遊子弟未遑學術，爽置館溫水之右，教授門徒七百餘人，京師學業，翕然復興。

translations.literal: At that time war chariots were repeatedly deployed and conquest was the business of the day; the sons of the nobility had no leisure for scholarship. Shuang established a school east of the Wen River and instructed more than seven hundred disciples, and learning in the capital suddenly revived.
translations.idiomatic: At that time campaigns followed one upon another and war was the order of the day; the sons of great families had no time for study. Shuang founded a school on the east bank of the Wen River and taught more than seven hundred disciples, and learning in the capital swiftly revived.

sentences.zh: 爽立訓甚有勸罰之科，弟子事之若嚴君焉。

translations.literal: Shuang's established teachings included strict rules of reward and punishment, and his disciples served him as they would a stern master.
translations.idiomatic: The rules Shuang set down included clear rewards and punishments, and his disciples served him as they would a strict father.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射元贊、平原太守司馬真安、著作郎程靈虬，皆是爽教所就。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuan Zan, Administrator of Pingyuan Sima Zhen'an, and Editing Gentleman Cheng Lingqiu were all products of Shuang's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuan Zan, Administrator of Pingyuan Sima Zhen'an, and Editing Gentleman Cheng Lingqiu were all trained under Shuang.

sentences.zh: 崔浩、高允並稱爽之嚴教，奬厲有方。

translations.literal: Cui Hao and Gao Yun both praised Shuang's strict teaching and his skillful encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao and Gao Yun both praised Shuang's rigorous teaching and his effective methods of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「文翁柔勝，先生剛克，立教雖殊，成人一也。

translations.literal: Gao Yun said, "Wen Weng prevailed through softness; the Master prevails through firmness. Though the methods of establishing teaching differ, the making of adults is one."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun said, "Wen Weng prevailed through gentleness; the Master prevails through firmness. Their ways of establishing a school differ, yet both succeed in shaping mature men."

sentences.zh: 」其為通識歎服如此。

translations.literal: Such was the admiration in which men of comprehensive learning held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the admiration he won from men of broad and deep learning.

sentences.zh: 因教授之暇，述六經略注，以廣制作，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: In the intervals of teaching he composed Brief Notes on the Six Classics to expand the corpus of written works, and they were very systematic.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time from teaching he wrote Brief Notes on the Six Classics to enlarge the body of scholarly work, and they were admirably well ordered.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：「傳稱：『立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。

translations.literal: Its preface says, "Tradition states: 'Establishing Heaven's Way is yin and yang; establishing Earth's Way is soft and hard; establishing Man's Way is benevolence and righteousness.'"
translations.idiomatic: Its preface reads: "Tradition says, 'Establishing Heaven's Way means yin and yang; establishing Earth's Way means soft and hard; establishing Man's Way means benevolence and righteousness.'"

sentences.zh: 』然則仁義者人之性也，經典者身之文也，皆以陶鑄神情，啟悟耳目，未有不由學而能成其器，不由習而能利其業。

translations.literal: "Thus benevolence and righteousness are human nature, and the classics are the adornment of the person; both are meant to mold spirit and sentiment and to open the ears and eyes. None achieves full capacity without learning, and none brings profit to his craft without practice."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus benevolence and righteousness belong to human nature, and the classics are the cultivation of the person; both serve to shape the spirit and awaken the mind. No one completes his capacity without study, and no one perfects his work without practice."

sentences.zh: 是故季路勇士也，服道以成忠烈之概；

translations.literal: "Therefore Zilu was a warrior, yet by submitting to the Way he achieved the stature of loyal heroism;"
translations.idiomatic: "Zilu was a man of force, yet by embracing the Way he attained the stature of loyal heroism;"

sentences.zh: 甯越庸夫也，講藝以全高尚之節。

translations.literal: "Ning Yue was a common man, yet by studying the arts he preserved a lofty integrity."
translations.idiomatic: "Ning Yue was an ordinary man, yet by pursuing learning he preserved a noble integrity."

sentences.zh: 蓋所由者習也，所因者本也，本立而道生，身文而德備焉。

translations.literal: "What one follows is practice; what one relies on is the root. When the root is established the Way arises; when the person is adorned, virtue is complete."
translations.idiomatic: "What one follows is practice; what one relies on is the foundation. When the foundation is set, the Way emerges; when the person is cultivated, virtue is complete."

sentences.zh: 昔者先王之訓天下也，莫不導以詩書，教以禮樂，移其風俗，和其人民。

translations.literal: "Formerly, when the sage kings instructed all under Heaven, none failed to guide them with the Poetry and Documents, teach them with Rites and Music, transform their customs, and harmonize their people."
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity, when the sage kings instructed all under Heaven, they always guided the people with the Poetry and Documents, taught them with Rites and Music, transformed their customs, and brought their people into harmony."

sentences.zh: 故恭儉莊敬而不煩者，教深於禮也；

translations.literal: "Thus to be reverent, frugal, dignified, and respectful without weariness is teaching rooted deeply in the Rites;"
translations.idiomatic: "To be reverent, frugal, dignified, and respectful without becoming weary—that is teaching rooted deeply in the Rites;"

sentences.zh: 廣博易良而不奢者，教深於樂也；

translations.literal: "to be broad, easy, and good without extravagance is teaching rooted deeply in Music;"
translations.idiomatic: "to be broad-minded, approachable, and good without falling into excess—that is teaching rooted deeply in Music;"

sentences.zh: 溫柔敦厚而不愚者，教深於詩也；

translations.literal: "to be gentle, soft, sincere, and generous without foolishness is teaching rooted deeply in the Poetry;"
translations.idiomatic: "to be gentle, sincere, and generous without becoming foolish—that is teaching rooted deeply in the Poetry;"

sentences.zh: 疏通知遠而不誣者，教深於書也；

translations.literal: "to be penetrating, discerning, and far-reaching without deception is teaching rooted deeply in the Documents;"
translations.idiomatic: "to be penetrating, discerning, and far-sighted without deceit—that is teaching rooted deeply in the Documents;"

sentences.zh: 潔靜精微而不賊者，教深於易也；

translations.literal: "to be pure, still, subtle, and precise without harm is teaching rooted deeply in the Changes;"
translations.idiomatic: "to be pure, still, subtle, and precise without doing injury—that is teaching rooted deeply in the Changes;"

sentences.zh: 屬辭比事而不亂者，教深於春秋也。

translations.literal: "to connect words and compare affairs without disorder is teaching rooted deeply in the Spring and Autumn."
translations.idiomatic: "to connect language with events and compare cases without confusion—that is teaching rooted deeply in the Spring and Autumn Annals."

sentences.zh: 夫樂以和神，詩以正言，禮以明體，書以廣聽，春秋以斷事，五者蓋五常之道相須而備，而易為之源。

translations.literal: Now, music is to harmonize the spirit; the Odes to rectify speech; ritual to clarify the bodily form; the Documents to broaden the ear; Spring and Autumn to decide affairs—the five are the Way of the five constants, mutually needing and completing one another, and the Changes is their source.
translations.idiomatic: Music harmonizes the spirit; the Book of Songs sets language right; ritual clarifies conduct; the Documents widen one's hearing; Spring and Autumn passes judgment on affairs. These five embody the Way of the five constants, each indispensable to the rest—and the Book of Changes is their wellspring.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「易不可見則乾坤其幾乎息矣。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "If the Changes cannot be seen, then Heaven and Earth would almost cease, would they not?
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "If the Changes cannot be seen, Heaven and Earth would nearly fall still.

sentences.zh: 」由是言之，六經者先王之遺烈，聖人之盛事也。

translations.literal: " From this it follows that the Six Classics are the enduring achievements left by the former kings, the grand undertakings of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: " From this it follows that the Six Classics are the lasting legacy of the ancient kings—the supreme work of the sages.

sentences.zh: 安可不遊心寓目，習性文身哉！

translations.literal: How could one fail to roam the mind and lodge the eye therein, habituating one's nature and adorning one's person!
translations.idiomatic: How could one not give one's heart and eyes to them, shaping character and refining the self!

sentences.zh: 頃因暇日，屬意藝林，略撰所聞，討論其本，名曰六經略注以訓門徒焉。

translations.literal: Recently, on days of leisure, I turned my attention to the grove of arts, briefly setting down what I had heard and discussing their roots, titling it Outline Commentary on the Six Classics to instruct my disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, in idle hours, I devoted myself to the forest of learning, sketching what I had heard and probing their foundations. I called the work Brief Notes on the Six Classics, to train my disciples.

sentences.zh: 」其略注行於世。

translations.literal: " His outline commentary circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " His Brief Notes circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 爽不事王侯，獨守閑靜，講肄經典二十餘年，時人號為「儒林先生」。

translations.literal: Shuang did not serve princes or marquises; he alone kept to quiet seclusion, lecturing and studying the classics for more than twenty years, and men of the age styled him "Master of the Confucian Grove."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang would not attend on princes or nobles. He lived apart in quiet, lecturing on the classics for more than twenty years, until contemporaries called him Master of the Confucian Grove.

sentences.zh: 年六十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty-three, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 子文通，歷官至鎮西司馬、南天水太守、西翼校尉。

translations.literal: His son Wentong rose through offices to General Who Stabilizes the West, Administrator of Southern Tianshui, and Colonel of the Western Wing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wentong served in turn as General Who Stabilizes the West, Administrator of Southern Tianshui, and Colonel of the Western Wing.

sentences.zh: 文通子景，別有傳。

translations.literal: Wentong's son Jing has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong's son Jing is treated in another biography.

sentences.zh: 劉獻之，博陵饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xianzhi was a man of Raoyang in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xianzhi came from Raoyang in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 少而孤貧，雅好詩、傳，曾受業於勃海程玄，後遂博觀眾籍。

translations.literal: From youth he was orphaned and poor; he loved the Odes and the chronicle, once studied under Cheng Xuan of Bohai, and afterward read widely in many texts.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from boyhood, he cherished the Odes and the chronicle tradition. He studied under Cheng Xuan of Bohai, then ranged widely through the canon.

sentences.zh: 見名法之言，掩卷而笑曰：「若使楊墨之流不為此書，千載誰知其小也！

translations.literal: Seeing legalist sayings, he would close the scroll and laugh, saying: "If followers of Yang and Mo had not written this book, who after a thousand years would know their pettiness!
translations.idiomatic: When he came upon the words of the legalists, he would shut the book and laugh: "Had the Yang and Mo schools never penned this text, who a thousand years hence would know how small they were?

sentences.zh: 」曾謂其所親曰：「觀屈原離騷之作，自是狂人，死其宜矣，何足惜也！

translations.literal: " Once he said to those close to him: "Reading Qu Yuan's Encountering Sorrow, one sees he was a madman from the start; his death was fitting—what is there to regret!
translations.idiomatic: " He once told his intimates: "Read Qu Yuan's Encountering Sorrow and you see a madman from the first. He deserved to die—why mourn him?

sentences.zh: 吾常謂濯纓洗耳，有異人之迹；

translations.literal: I have often said that washing the tassel and washing the ear bear the traces of uncommon men;
translations.idiomatic: I have always thought that washing the cap-tassel and washing the ears belong to men apart from the world;

sentences.zh: 哺糟歠醨，有同物之志。

translations.literal: feeding on lees and drinking the dregs shows a mind kin with the common creature.
translations.idiomatic: while feeding on dregs and drinking the sour lees shows a spirit at one with the herd.

sentences.zh: 而孔子曰：『我則異於是，無可無不可。

translations.literal: Yet Confucius said: "I am different from this—neither insisting nor refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Confucius said, "As for me, I am not like that—I may go either way, or neither.

sentences.zh: 』誠哉斯言，實獲我心。」

translations.literal: " Truly those words hit home—they are exactly what my heart holds."
translations.idiomatic: " How true that is—it is precisely what I feel."

sentences.zh: 時人有從獻之學者，獻之輒謂之曰：「人之立身，雖百行殊途，準之四科，要以德行為首。

translations.literal: When someone came to study with Xianzhi, he would always tell them: "In establishing oneself, though the hundred paths differ, measured by the four categories, virtuous conduct must come first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone sought instruction from Xianzhi, he would say: "To stand in the world, the hundred paths may diverge, but judged by the four categories of the sage, moral conduct must lead.

sentences.zh: 君若能入孝出悌，忠信仁讓，不待出戶，天下自知。

translations.literal: If you can be filial at home and respectful abroad, loyal, trustworthy, benevolent, and yielding, without waiting to leave your door the world will know you.
translations.idiomatic: If you can be filial within and deferential without—loyal, trustworthy, humane, and modest—the world will know you before you step outside.

sentences.zh: 儻不能然，雖復下帷針股，躡屩從師，正可博聞多識，不過為土龍乞雨，眩惑將來，其於立身之道有何益乎？

translations.literal: If not, though you draw the curtain and pierce your thigh with a needle, tread in straw sandals to follow teachers, you may only broaden hearsay—it is no better than a clay dragon praying for rain, dazzling those yet to come. What good does that do for the Way of establishing oneself?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot, then even if you study behind closed curtains, jab your thigh to stay awake, and chase after masters in straw shoes, you will merely amass facts—no better than a clay dragon invoked for rain, fooling generations yet unborn. What profit is that for the art of living?

sentences.zh: 孔門之徒，初亦未悟，見臯魚之歎，方歸而養親。

translations.literal: Confucius's disciples too at first did not understand; only when they saw Gaoyu's lament did they return home to care for their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Even the followers of Confucius did not grasp this at first; only after Gaoyu's lament did they go home to nourish their parents.

sentences.zh: [4]嗟乎先達，何自覺之晚也！

translations.literal: Alas, you who have gone before—why did you wake to this so late!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, you elders of the past—why did you see it only so late!

sentences.zh: 束脩不易，受之亦難，敢布心腹，子其圖之。

translations.literal: A bundle of dried meat is not lightly exchanged, nor is receiving instruction easy. I dare lay bare my inmost thoughts—take them to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The gift of dried meat is not given lightly, nor is it easy to receive such teaching. I speak frankly from the heart—ponder it well.

sentences.zh: 」由是四方學者莫不高其行義而希造其門。

translations.literal: " From this, scholars from all quarters held his conduct in esteem and longed to reach his gate.
translations.idiomatic: " After this, learners everywhere admired his integrity and yearned to study at his door.

sentences.zh: 獻之善春秋、毛詩，每講左氏，盡隱公八年便止，云義例已了，不復須解。

translations.literal: Xianzhi excelled in Spring and Autumn and the Mao Odes. Whenever he lectured on the Zuo tradition, he stopped entirely at the eighth year of Duke Yin, saying the principles and examples were complete and no further gloss was needed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was master of Spring and Autumn and the Mao version of the Odes. In lecturing on the Zuo commentary he always ended at the eighth year of Duke Yin, declaring the pattern of meaning complete and further explanation unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 由是弟子不能究竟其說。

translations.literal: Thus his disciples could not fully master his teachings.
translations.idiomatic: His students therefore could never exhaust his doctrine.

sentences.zh: 後本郡舉孝廉，非其好也，逼遣之，乃應命，至京，稱疾而還。

translations.literal: Later the commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt—a course he did not relish. Pressed, he accepted; upon reaching the capital he pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later his commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, which did not suit his taste. They forced him to go; he obeyed, but once he reached the capital he claimed illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸中山，詔徵典內校書，獻之喟然歎曰：「吾不如莊周散木遠矣！

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu visited Zhongshan, an edict summoned him to oversee collation within the palace. Xianzhi sighed deeply: "How far I fall short of Zhuang Zhou's useless stump!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu toured Zhongshan, an edict called him to supervise collation in the inner archives. Xianzhi sighed: "I am nothing like Zhuang Zhou's worthless timber!

sentences.zh: 一之謂甚，其可再乎。

translations.literal: Once is already too much—how could it happen again?
translations.idiomatic: To be cut once is already too much—how could it happen twice?

sentences.zh: 」固以疾辭。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " He steadfastly refused, pleading sickness.

sentences.zh: 時中山張吾貴與獻之齊名，海內皆曰儒宗。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan shared fame with Xianzhi; throughout the realm both were called patriarchs of learning.
translations.idiomatic: In those days Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan stood equal in renown with Xianzhi; across the empire both were hailed as pillars of Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 吾貴每一講唱，門徒千數，其行業可稱者寡。

translations.literal: Whenever Wugui lectured, his disciples numbered in the thousands, yet few of them possessed conduct or achievement worth naming.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Wugui held forth, a thousand students gathered, but scarcely any among them had conduct or accomplishment worth mention.

sentences.zh: 獻之著錄，數百而已，皆經通之士。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's registered students numbered only in the hundreds, and all were masters who had penetrated the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's roster held only a few hundred names, every one a scholar who had truly mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 於是有識者辨其優劣。

translations.literal: Thereupon men of discernment distinguished their relative merit.
translations.idiomatic: Perceptive observers therefore judged which of the two was superior.

sentences.zh: 魏承喪亂之後，五經大義雖有師說，而海內諸生多有疑滯，咸決於獻之。

translations.literal: Wei, inheriting an age of chaos, still had teacher-traditions for the great meaning of the Five Classics, yet scholars everywhere harbored many doubts—and all were resolved by Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei state, rising after generations of turmoil, preserved oral traditions of the Five Classics, yet students throughout the land remained tangled in doubt—and Xianzhi settled every question.

sentences.zh: 六藝之文，雖不悉注，然所標宗旨，頗異舊義，撰三禮大義四卷，三傳略例三卷，注毛詩序義一卷，今行於世，并章句疏三卷。
