translations.literal: Though he did not comment exhaustively on the texts of the six arts, the principles he marked often differed from older interpretations. He compiled Great Meaning of the Three Rites in four juan, Brief Models of the Three Commentaries in three juan, and Commentary on the Prefaces of the Mao Odes in one juan—all current in his day—along with three juan of chapter-and-clause commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He did not annotate every line of the six arts, yet the doctrines he emphasized often broke with received opinion. He wrote Great Meaning of the Three Rites in four scrolls, Brief Patterns of the Three Commentaries in three scrolls, and Notes on the Prefaces of the Mao Odes in one scroll, all still in circulation, together with three scrolls of glosses on individual passages.

sentences.zh: 注湼槃經未就而卒。

translations.literal: He was annotating the Nirvana Sutra when death came before he finished.
translations.idiomatic: He was midway through a commentary on the Nirvana Sutra when he died.

sentences.zh: 有四子，放古、爰古、參古、脩古。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Fanggu, Aigu, Cangu, and Xiugu.
translations.idiomatic: He left four sons—Fanggu, Aigu, Cangu, and Xiugu.

sentences.zh: 放古，幼有人才。

translations.literal: Fanggu showed talent from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Fanggu was gifted even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 為州從事，早亡。

translations.literal: He served as a provincial aide and died young.
translations.idiomatic: He became a commandery staff officer and died early.

sentences.zh: 爰古、參古，並傳父詩而不能精通也。

translations.literal: Aigu and Cangu both transmitted their father's Odes but could not master them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Aigu and Cangu carried on their father's teaching of the Odes but never attained his depth.

sentences.zh: 張吾貴，字吳子，中山人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wugui, courtesy name Wuzi, was from Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wugui, styled Wuzi, was a native of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 少聰惠口辯，身長八尺，容貌奇偉。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and eloquent; he stood eight chi tall, with a striking, imposing countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick-tongued from boyhood, he stood eight feet tall, with a singular, commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 年十八，本郡舉為太學博士。

translations.literal: At eighteen his commandery recommended him as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen his commandery presented him as a doctoral lecturer at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 吾貴先未多學，乃從酈詮受禮，牛天祐受易。

translations.literal: Wugui had not studied widely at first; he received Rites from Li Quan and Changes from Niu Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui had not read deeply at first. He took Rites from Li Quan and the Changes from Niu Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 詮、祐粗為開發，而吾貴覽讀一遍，便即別構戶牖。

translations.literal: Quan and You gave him only a rough opening—yet Wugui read through once and at once erected gates and windows of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and You merely opened the door for him, but Wugui read each text once and immediately built a structure of his own.

sentences.zh: 世人競歸之。

translations.literal: The world rushed to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 曾在夏學，聚徒千數而不講傳，生徒竊云張生之於左氏似不能說。

translations.literal: Once during the summer academy he gathered a thousand disciples yet lectured on no commentary; students whispered that Master Zhang seemed unable to expound the Zuo tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at the summer school, he assembled a thousand pupils but never expounded any commentary. His students murmured that Zhang seemed unable to lecture on the Zuo tradition.

sentences.zh: 吾貴聞之，謂其徒曰：「我今夏講暫罷，後當說傳，君等來日皆當持本。

translations.literal: Wugui heard this and told them: "This summer's lectures are halted for now; later I shall expound the commentary—you must all bring your texts tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui heard the talk and told his followers: "I am pausing lectures for the summer. Next I will expound the commentary—you must all bring your books tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」生徒怪之而已。

translations.literal: " The disciples marveled but said nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: " The students were puzzled but waited.

sentences.zh: 吾貴謂劉蘭云：「君曾讀左氏，為我一說。

translations.literal: Wugui said to Liu Lan: "You have read the Zuo tradition—expound it for me once.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui said to Liu Lan, "You have studied the Zuo commentary—lecture it for me.

sentences.zh: 」蘭遂為講。

translations.literal: " Lan then lectured.
translations.idiomatic: " Lan did so.

sentences.zh: 三旬之中，吾貴兼讀杜、服，隱括兩家，異同悉舉。

translations.literal: Within thirty days Wugui read both Du and Fu, distilled the two schools, and set forth every point of agreement and difference.
translations.idiomatic: In thirty days Wugui read both Du Yu and Fu Qian, trimmed and compared the two houses, and noted every agreement and divergence.

sentences.zh: 諸生後集，便為講之，義例無窮，皆多新異。

translations.literal: When the students assembled afterward, he lectured at once—principles and patterns without end, mostly fresh and novel.
translations.idiomatic: When the students gathered again, he lectured immediately—principles without limit, mostly new and startling.

sentences.zh: 蘭乃伏聽。

translations.literal: Lan listened prone in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Lan listened, prostrate with admiration.

sentences.zh: 學者以此益奇之。

translations.literal: Scholars therefore marveled at him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The scholarly world wondered at him all the more.

sentences.zh: 而以辯能飾非，好為詭說，由是業不久傳，而氣陵牧守，不屈王侯，竟不仕而終。

translations.literal: Yet because he could argue to paper over faults and loved strange doctrines, his teaching did not long endure; haughty toward governors and prefects, he would not bow to princes or marquises, and in the end never took office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he used debate to gloss over error and delighted in paradox, so his school did not last. Overbearing toward local officials, refusing to yield to nobles, he never held office and died as he had lived.

sentences.zh: 劉蘭，武邑人。

translations.literal: Liu Lan was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lan came from Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，始入小學，書急就篇。

translations.literal: Past thirty he first entered elementary study, copying the Rapid Composition Primer.
translations.idiomatic: Not until his thirties did he begin elementary schooling, practicing the Rapid Composition Primer.

sentences.zh: 家人覺其聰敏，遂令從師，受春秋、詩、禮於中山王保安。

translations.literal: His family saw his keenness and sent him to study; he received Spring and Autumn, the Odes, and Rites from Wang Bao'an of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His kin noticed his sharp mind and sent him to teachers. From Wang Bao'an of Zhongshan he learned Spring and Autumn, the Odes, and Rites.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以自資，且耕且學。

translations.literal: Poor at home with no means to support himself, he farmed and studied by turns.
translations.idiomatic: His household was destitute; he alternated plowing with study.

sentences.zh: 三年之後，便白其兄：「蘭欲講書。

translations.literal: After three years he told his elder brother: "Lan wishes to lecture on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he told his elder brother, "Lan wants to teach the classics.

sentences.zh: 」其兄笑而聽之，為立黌舍，聚徒二百。

translations.literal: " His brother laughed but agreed, built a schoolhouse, and gathered two hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: " His brother laughed but indulged him, built a hall, and enrolled two hundred students.

sentences.zh: 蘭讀左氏，五日一遍，兼通五經。

translations.literal: Lan read the Zuo tradition through once every five days and mastered all five classics besides.
translations.idiomatic: Lan read through the Zuo commentary every five days and came to know all five classics.

sentences.zh: 先是張吾貴以聰辨過人，其所解說，不本先儒之旨。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Wugui's quick wit surpassed others, but his explications did not rest on the intent of prior Ru masters.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Zhang Wugui's brilliance outshone others, yet his interpretations did not anchor in the old masters.

sentences.zh: 唯蘭推經、傳之由，本注者之意，參以緯候及先儒舊事，甚為精悉。

translations.literal: Lan alone traced the grounds of classic and commentary, rooted in the commentators' intent, cross-checked with weft-texts, calendrical signs, and old Ru traditions—most precise and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Lan alone traced how classic and commentary fit together, staying true to the commentators' purpose and weighing apocryphal texts, omens, and earlier Ru lore—work of rare precision.

sentences.zh: 自後經義審博，皆由於蘭。

translations.literal: Afterward, thorough mastery of classical meaning owed everything to Lan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, deep learning in the classics flowed from Lan.

sentences.zh: 蘭又明陰陽，博物多識，為儒者所宗。

translations.literal: Lan also understood yin and yang, knew much of the natural world, and was revered among Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He also understood yin and yang, knew nature's myriad forms, and was honored among Confucians.

sentences.zh: 瀛州刺史裴植徵蘭講書於州城南館，植為學主，故生徒甚盛，海內稱焉。

translations.literal: Pei Zhi, Inspector of Yingzhou, summoned Lan to lecture at the south hall of the province; Zhi served as patron of the school, so disciples flourished and the realm took note.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi, governor of Ying province, invited Lan to teach at the south lodge of the prefectural seat. Zhi acted as patron, the student body swelled, and fame spread across the land.

sentences.zh: 又特為中山王英所重。

translations.literal: He was especially esteemed by Prince Ying of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Zhongshan held him in particular regard.

sentences.zh: 英引在館，令授其子熙、誘、略等。

translations.literal: Ying brought him into his household and had him instruct his sons Xi, You, Lue, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ying kept him in residence and set him to teach his sons Xi, You, Lue, and the others.

sentences.zh: 蘭學徒前後數千，成業者眾，而排毀公羊，又非董仲舒，由是見譏於世。

translations.literal: Lan's disciples numbered thousands over the years and many completed their training; yet because he rejected and denigrated the Gongyang tradition and also disparaged Dong Zhongshu, he was mocked by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands passed through Lan's school and many finished their training, but he attacked the Gongyang commentary and belittled Dong Zhongshu, and for this the world scorned him.

sentences.zh: 永平中，為國子助教。

translations.literal: During Yongping he served as assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era he was assistant lecturer at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，靜坐讀書，有人叩門，門人通焉，蘭命引入。

translations.literal: During Yanxing he sat quietly reading when someone knocked; a disciple announced him and Lan ordered him brought in.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanxing era, as he sat reading in silence, someone knocked. A pupil reported the visitor and Lan bade him enter.

sentences.zh: 其人葛巾單衣，入與蘭坐，謂蘭曰：「君自是學士，何為每見毀辱，理義長短，竟知在誰，而過無禮見陵也。

translations.literal: The man wore a hemp cap and plain robe, entered and sat with Lan, and said: "You are a scholar—why do you suffer insult time and again? Who truly holds the long and short of principle we know—but you are overborne without courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The stranger wore a hemp headcloth and single-layer robe. He came in, sat beside Lan, and said: "You are a man of learning—why do you endure such abuse? We know whose reasoning stands and whose falls—yet you are trampled without respect.

sentences.zh: 今欲相召，當與君正之。

translations.literal: I wish to summon you now; I shall set this right with you.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to summon you now and settle the matter with you.

sentences.zh: 」言終而出。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he went out.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he left.

sentences.zh: 出後，蘭告家人。

translations.literal: After he left, Lan told his family.
translations.idiomatic: When the man was gone, Lan described the visit to his household.

sentences.zh: 少時而患卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 孫惠蔚，字叔炳，武邑武遂人也，小字陀羅。

translations.literal: Sun Huiwei, courtesy name Shubing, was from Wusui in Wuyi; his childhood name was Tuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huiwei, styled Shubing, came from Wusui in Wuyi; his pet name was Tuoluo.

sentences.zh: 自言六世祖道恭為晉長秋卿，自道恭至惠蔚世以儒學相傳。

translations.literal: He said his sixth-generation ancestor Dao Gong had been Director of Palace Attendants under Jin; from Dao Gong to Huiwei the family transmitted learning through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: He traced six generations back to Dao Gong, Director of Palace Attendants under Jin; from Dao Gong to Huiwei the family handed down Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚年十三，粗通詩、書及孝經、論語；

translations.literal: At thirteen Huiwei had a rough grasp of the Odes, Documents, Filial Classic, and Analects;
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Huiwei had a working knowledge of the Odes, Documents, Filial Classic, and Analects;

sentences.zh: 十八，師董道季講易；

translations.literal: at eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji;
translations.idiomatic: at eighteen he studied the Changes with Dong Daoji;

sentences.zh: 十九，師程玄讀禮經及春秋三傳。

translations.literal: at nineteen he read the Ritual Canon and the three Spring-and-Autumn commentaries under Cheng Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: at nineteen he read the Ritual Canon and the three commentaries on Spring and Autumn under Cheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 周流儒肆，有名於冀方。

translations.literal: He moved among Confucian academies and was known in the Ji region.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled the halls of learning and was known throughout Ji province.

sentences.zh: 太和初，郡舉孝廉，對策於中書省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe the commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; he answered policy questions at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign his commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt; he sat for the palace examination at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時中書監高閭宿聞惠蔚，稱其英辯，因相談，薦為中書博士。

translations.literal: Secretary-Director Gao Lu had long heard of Huiwei and praised his keen eloquence; they conversed, and Lu recommended him as Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu, Director of the Secretariat, had long known of Huiwei's brilliance and praised his sharp speech. After they talked, Lu recommended him as a Secretariat erudite.

sentences.zh: 轉皇宗博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to erudite of the imperial clan school.

sentences.zh: 閭被敕理定雅樂，惠蔚參其事。

translations.literal: Lu was ordered to arrange and fix the court music; Huiwei took part.
translations.idiomatic: Lu received orders to codify the court ritual music, and Huiwei assisted.

sentences.zh: 及樂成，閭上疏請集朝貴於太樂，共研是非。

translations.literal: When the music was finished, Lu memorialized asking that court nobles assemble at the Grand Music Office to weigh right and wrong together.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was complete, Lu submitted a memorial asking that high officials gather at the Music Bureau to debate what was correct.

sentences.zh: 祕書令李彪自以才辯，立難於其間，閭命惠蔚與彪抗論，彪不能屈。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his wit, raised objections in the midst; Lu ordered Huiwei to debate Biao—and Biao could not make him yield.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao, Director of the Secretariat, trusting his own eloquence, challenged the work on the spot. Lu had Huiwei answer him—and Biao could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎張彝常與遊處，每表疏論事，多參訪焉。

translations.literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate Zhang Yi often kept company with him; whenever Yi memorialized on affairs of state he frequently sought Huiwei's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, Attendant at the Yellow Gate, often kept his company; when Yi drafted memorials on state affairs he consulted Huiwei.

sentences.zh: 十七年，高祖南征，上議告類之禮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Emperor Gaozu marched south, the court debated the rites of announcing victory to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, during Emperor Gaozu's southern campaign, the court deliberated the rites of reporting victory to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 及太師馮熙薨，惠蔚監其喪禮，上書令熙未冠之子皆服成人之服。

translations.literal: When Grand Preceptor Feng Xi died, Huiwei oversaw the mourning rites and memorialized that Xi's sons not yet capped should wear the garb of full adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Preceptor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised the funeral rites and memorialized that Xi's sons, though not yet capped, should wear adult mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚與李彪以儒學相知，及彪位至尚書，惠蔚仍太廟令。

translations.literal: Huiwei and Li Biao knew each other through their shared learning; when Biao rose to Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei and Li Biao were friends in the classics; when Biao advanced to Minister of the Secretariat, Huiwei still held the modest post of Director of the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾從容言曰：「道固既登龍門而孫蔚猶沉涓澮，朕常以為負矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once said at leisure: "Dao Gu has already crossed the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei still sinks in the shallows—I have always felt this a failing on my part.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once remarked casually: "Dao Gu has leapt the Dragon Gate, yet Sun Wei still lingers in the shallows—I have always felt ashamed of that.

sentences.zh: 」雖久滯小官，深體通塞，無孜孜之望，儒者以是尚焉。

translations.literal: " Though long stuck in minor posts, he deeply understood advance and obstruction and nursed no restless ambition; for this Confucian scholars held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: " Though he languished in low office, he understood fortune and setback and never burned with ambition; Confucians admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，侍讀東宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as lecturer in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became reader to the crown prince in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是七廟以平文為太祖，高祖議定祖宗，以道武為太祖。

translations.literal: Previously the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founding Ancestor; Emperor Gaozu deliberated on the founding line and made Emperor Daowu Founding Ancestor instead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the seven ancestral temples had honored Emperor Pingwen as founding ancestor; Emperor Gaozu reconsidered the imperial line and set Emperor Daowu as founding ancestor instead.

sentences.zh: 祖宗雖定，然昭穆未改。

translations.literal: Although the founding line had been settled, the zhao-mu order in the ancestral temple had not yet been adjusted.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial ancestors had been fixed, but the left-right ordering of spirit tablets in the temple had not yet been changed.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，祔神主於廟，時侍中崔光兼太常卿，以太祖既改，昭穆以次而易。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died and his spirit tablet was enshrined in the temple, Cui Guang, Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Minister of Ceremonies, held that since the Founding Ancestor title had been changed, the zhao-mu sequence should shift accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death, when his spirit tablet was placed in the ancestral temple, Secretariat Director Cui Guang, who also served as Minister of Ceremonies, argued that with the change of founding ancestor the zhao-mu order should be rearranged in sequence.

sentences.zh: 兼御史中尉、黃門侍郎邢巒以為太祖雖改，昭穆仍不應易，乃立彈草欲按奏光。

translations.literal: Concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Palace Attendant Xing Luan held that although the Founding Ancestor had been changed, the zhao-mu order should still not be altered; he drafted a memorial of impeachment intending to press charges against Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief and Palace Attendant Xing Luan maintained that even though the founding ancestor had changed, the zhao-mu arrangement ought not to shift; he prepared an impeachment draft to accuse Guang.

sentences.zh: 光謂惠蔚曰：「此乃禮也，而執法欲見彈劾，思獲助於碩學。

translations.literal: Guang said to Huiwei, "This is a matter of ritual propriety, yet the law officer wishes to impeach me; I hope to gain support from a leading scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Guang told Huiwei, "This is ritual law, but the enforcement official wants to impeach me—I am looking to you, as a master of learning, for support."

sentences.zh: 」惠蔚曰：「此深得禮變。

translations.literal: Huiwei said, "This accords deeply with ritual adaptation."
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei replied, "That reading fits the principle of adapting ritual to changed circumstances."

sentences.zh: 」尋為書以與光，讚明其事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he wrote a letter to Guang, clarifying and praising the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent Guang a letter explaining the case and endorsing his view.

sentences.zh: 光以惠蔚書呈宰輔，乃召惠蔚與巒庭議得失，尚書令王肅又助巒，而巒理終屈，彈事遂寢。

translations.literal: Guang presented Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers, then summoned Huiwei and Luan to debate the rights and wrongs in court; Minister of Works Wang Su again sided with Luan, but Luan's argument was ultimately defeated and the impeachment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers and called Huiwei and Luan to argue the issue at court; Wang Su, head of the Ministry of Works, again backed Luan, yet Luan lost the debate and the impeachment came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位之後，仍在左右敷訓經典，自冗從僕射遷祕書丞、武邑郡中正。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shizong took the throne, Huiwei remained at his side instructing him in the classics; he was promoted from Supernumerary Vice Director of the Retainers to Secretary of the Secretariat and Rectifier of Wuoyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shizong acceded, Huiwei still attended him to expound the classics; he rose from supernumerary vice director of the retinue to secretary in the imperial library and commandery rectifier for Wuoyi.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚既入東觀，見典籍未周，乃上疏曰：「臣聞聖皇之御世也，必幽贊人經，參天二地，憲章典故，述遵鴻猷。

translations.literal: After Huiwei entered the Eastern Pavilion, he saw that the canonical collections were incomplete and submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that when a sage emperor governs the age, he must secretly assist the human classics, take heaven and earth as his model, take ancient statutes as his charter, and follow the great design."
translations.idiomatic: Having entered the Eastern Pavilion, Huiwei found the library holdings incomplete and memorialized: "I understand that a sage ruler in governing the world inwardly upholds the human classics, models himself on heaven and earth, takes precedent as law, and follows the grand plan."

sentences.zh: 故易曰：『觀乎天文以察時變，觀乎人文以化成天下。

translations.literal: Thus the Changes says: 'Contemplate the patterns of heaven to discern the seasons' changes; contemplate the patterns of human affairs to transform and perfect all under heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 'Look to the heavens to observe seasonal change; look to human culture to transform the realm.'

sentences.zh: 』然則六經、百氏，圖書祕籍，乃承天之正術，治人之貞範。

translations.literal: Then the Six Classics and the hundred schools, books and secret archives, are the orthodox arts handed down by heaven and the steadfast norms for governing men.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics, the hundred philosophers, books and secret texts are heaven's proper arts and the enduring standards for ruling people.

sentences.zh: 是以溫柔疏遠，詩書之教；

translations.literal: Hence gentle remoteness is the teaching of Poetry and Documents;
translations.idiomatic: Thus through gentle distance come the teachings of the Odes and Documents;

sentences.zh: 恭儉易良，禮樂之道。

translations.literal: respectful thrift, ease, and goodness are the way of Ritual and Music.
translations.idiomatic: respect, frugality, ease, and integrity are the path of Ritual and Music.

sentences.zh: 爻彖以精微為神，春秋以屬辭為化。

translations.literal: The line statements and judgments of the Changes take subtlety as their spirit; the Spring and Autumn Annals take linked wording as their transforming power.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes' component texts find their divinity in refinement; the Spring and Autumn achieves transformation through layered phrasing.

sentences.zh: 故大訓炳於東序，藝文光於麟閣。

translations.literal: Therefore the great instructions shine in the eastern gallery and literary works blaze in the Qilin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Great instruction blazes in the eastern hall; literary treasures gleam in the Qilin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 斯實太平之樞宗，勝殘之要道，有國之靈基，帝王之盛業。

translations.literal: This is truly the pivot of great peace, the essential path to overcoming cruelty, the numinous foundation of a state, and the supreme achievement of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: It is the hinge of great peace, the key to overcoming violence, the spiritual base of dynasties, and the crowning work of sage rulers.

sentences.zh: 安上靖民，敦風美俗，其在茲乎？

translations.literal: To settle superiors and pacify the people, to nurture custom and beautify manners—is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: Securing the throne and quieting the people, refining custom and elevating morals—does this not begin here?

sentences.zh: 及秦棄學術，禮經泯絕。

translations.literal: When Qin abandoned learning, the ritual classics perished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin, when scholarship was cast aside, the ritual canon was lost.

sentences.zh: 漢興求訪，典文載舉，先王遺訓，燦然復存。

translations.literal: When Han rose it sought them out; canonical texts were gathered again and the former kings' transmitted instructions shone once more.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, on rising, searched them out; canonical writings were collected anew and the sages' legacy lived again.

sentences.zh: 暨光武撥亂，日不暇給，而入洛之書二千餘兩。

translations.literal: By the time Emperor Guangwu restored order he had no leisure even for meals, yet the books brought into Luoyang numbered more than two thousand cartloads.
translations.idiomatic: Even Guangwu, amid rebellion, scarcely had time to eat, yet books entering Luoyang filled more than two thousand carts.

sentences.zh: 魏晉之世，尤重典墳，收亡集逸，九流咸備。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin times canonical libraries were especially prized; lost works were recovered and collected until all nine intellectual traditions were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin especially treasured the canon; gathering what had vanished, they restored the nine traditions.

sentences.zh: 觀其鳩閱史篇，訪購經論，紙竹所載，略盡無遺。

translations.literal: See how they assembled and reviewed historical writings and sought to purchase classics and treatises—what paper and bamboo recorded was nearly all preserved.
translations.idiomatic: They collated histories, bought classics and commentaries, and on paper and bamboo little was left missing.

sentences.zh: 臣學闕通儒，思不及遠，徒循章句，片義無立。

translations.literal: My learning falls short of the comprehensive ru; my thought does not reach far—I merely follow chapter and phrase and cannot stand on any broad principle.
translations.idiomatic: I am no comprehensive scholar; my vision is narrow—I can only follow lines and clauses and hold to no wider insight.

sentences.zh: 而慈造曲覃，厠班祕省，忝官承乏，唯書是司。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty's gracious creation has drawn me into the ranks of the secretariat; I hold office in default and have charge only of books.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty's grace placed me in the secret archive; I serve in a gap-filling post with books alone as my charge.

sentences.zh: 而觀、閣舊典，先無定目，新故雜糅，首尾不全。

translations.literal: Yet the old holdings of the Pavilion and Archive had no fixed catalogue beforehand; new and old were mixed together and beginnings and ends were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The Pavilion and Archive collections had never had a fixed catalogue; old and new were jumbled and many volumes lacked beginnings or ends.

sentences.zh: 有者累帙數十，無者曠年不寫。

translations.literal: Where copies existed they might run to dozens of fascicles; where none existed years might pass without copying.
translations.idiomatic: Some titles filled dozens of fascicles; others went years without being copied at all.

sentences.zh: 或篇第褫落，始末淪殘；

translations.literal: Some fascicles and sections were torn away and beginnings and ends were ruined;
translations.idiomatic: Some volumes lost sections; openings and closings were destroyed;

sentences.zh: 或文壞字誤，謬爛相屬。

translations.literal: some texts were damaged and characters wrong, errors and corruption linked one to another.
translations.idiomatic: others had broken text and mistaken characters, error piled on error.

sentences.zh: 篇目雖多，全定者少。

translations.literal: Though the titles were many, complete and settled copies were few.
translations.idiomatic: Titles were plentiful, but fully intact editions were rare.

sentences.zh: 臣今依前丞臣盧昶所撰甲乙新錄，欲裨殘補闕，損併有無，校練句讀，以為定本，次第均寫，永為常式。

translations.literal: I now follow the new catalogue in jia and yi compiled by my predecessor Director Lu Chang, intending to repair what is broken and fill what is missing, reduce and merge where there is duplication or lack, collate phrasing and punctuation to make a fixed text, copy it in order, and establish it as a permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to follow Director Lu Chang's new catalogue in jia and yi ranks—to mend gaps, merge redundancies, collate punctuation into a definitive edition, copy it in sequence, and fix it as the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 其省先無本者，廣加推尋，搜求令足。

translations.literal: For offices that previously had no copy, search should be broadened until holdings are sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Where a department lacks a text, search widely until the collection is complete.

sentences.zh: 然經記浩博，諸子紛綸，部帙既多，章篇紕繆，當非一二校書，歲月可了。

translations.literal: Yet the classics and records are vast and the various masters numerous; with so many fascicles and so many confused chapters, this cannot be finished by one or two collators in a year.
translations.idiomatic: The canon is vast and the philosophers many; with countless fascicles and tangled chapters, one or two collators cannot finish the work in a year.

sentences.zh: 今求令四門博士及在京儒生四十人，在祕書省專精校考，參定字義。

translations.literal: I now ask that forty erudites of the Four Gates and Confucian scholars in the capital be assigned to the Secretariat to specialize in collating and to fix the meaning of characters together.
translations.idiomatic: I request forty Four Gates erudites and capital scholars to work in the Secretariat full-time on collation and agreed readings.

sentences.zh: 如蒙聽許，則典文允正，羣書大集。

translations.literal: If this is approved, canonical texts will be made correct and the collected books will be fully assembled.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's consent, the canon will be set right and the library fully gathered.

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 又兼黃門侍郎，遷中散大夫，仍兼黃門。

translations.literal: He was also made concurrent Palace Attendant, promoted to Palace Counsellor, and still held the Palace Attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Palace Attendant, was promoted to palace counsellor, and retained that attendant appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，正黃門侍郎，代崔光為著作郎，才非文史，無所撰著，唯自披其傳注數行而已。

translations.literal: After some time he became regular Palace Attendant and replaced Cui Guang as Compiler; his talent was not for history and letters and he wrote nothing, save that he annotated his own biography in a few lines.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became regular palace attendant and succeeded Cui Guang as compiler; he lacked gift for historiography and produced nothing except a few lines of self-commentary on his biography.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒、祕書監，仍知史事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial University and Superintendent of the Secretariat, and still oversaw historical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the National University and superintendent of the Secretariat, still managing historical work.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年，追賞侍講之勞，封棗強縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yan chang his service as lecturer was rewarded retroactively; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zaoqiang with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan chang year two his lecturing service was rewarded; he received the barony of Zaoqiang with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，出為平東將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Suzong's reign he went out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong began his reign, Huiwei left the capital as general who pacifies the east and governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 還京，除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 魏初已來，儒生寒宦，惠蔚最為顯達。

translations.literal: Since the beginning of Wei, among Confucian scholars of humble office Huiwei had risen highest.
translations.idiomatic: From early Wei onward, no Confucian from a modest background had risen as high as Huiwei.

sentences.zh: 先單名蔚，正始中，侍講禁內，夜論佛經，有愜帝旨，詔使加「惠」，號惠蔚法師焉。

translations.literal: Earlier he had borne the single name Wei; in the Zhengshi era, lecturing within the inner palace, he discussed Buddhist sutras at night in a way that pleased the emperor, who ordered the character Hui ('kindness') added and styled him Dharma Master Huiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Wei alone, during Zhengshi he lectured in the inner palace; his nightly exposition of Buddhist sutras pleased the emperor, who added Hui to his name and called him Dharma Master Huiwei.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年卒于官，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shen gui he died in office at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Shen gui year one he died in office at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 賜帛五百匹，贈大將軍、[5]瀛州刺史，諡曰戴。

translations.literal: Five hundred bolts of silk were granted; he was posthumously given the Grand General's title and Governor of Ying Province, with posthumous name Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred bolts of silk; posthumously he was made grand general and governor of Ying, with posthumous name Dai.

sentences.zh: 子伯禮，襲封。

translations.literal: His son Bolí inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bolí succeeded to the fief.

sentences.zh: 伯禮善隸書。

translations.literal: Bolí was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Bolí excelled at clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 拜奉朝請、員外散騎侍郎、寧朔將軍、步兵校尉、國子博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace Cadre, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts as court gentleman for attendance, supernumerary palace cadre gentleman, general who pacifies the north, colonel of the footsoldiers, and national university erudite.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously general who assists the state and governor of Ba.

sentences.zh: 子產同，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chantong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chantong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 少有才學，早亡，時人惜之。

translations.literal: He had talent and learning from youth but died young; men of the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and learned from youth, he died early—to contemporaries' sorrow.

sentences.zh: 徐遵明，字子判，華陰人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zunming, courtesy name Zipan, was a man of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zunming, styled Zipan, came from Huayin.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，幼孤好學。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet tall, was orphaned young, and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet in height, orphaned early, he devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 年十七，隨鄉人毛靈和等詣山東求學。

translations.literal: At seventeen he followed fellow townsman Mao Linghe and others to Shandong to seek teachers.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he went east with townsman Mao Linghe and others to find masters.

sentences.zh: 至上黨，乃師屯留王聰，受毛詩、尚書、禮記。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangdang, he took Wang Cong of Tunliu as teacher and studied the Mao Odes, Documents, and Record of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangdang he studied the Mao Odes, Documents, and Record of Ritual under Wang Cong of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 一年，便辭聰詣燕趙，師事張吾貴。

translations.literal: After one year he left Cong and went to Yan and Zhao to study under Zhang Wugui.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he left Cong for Yan and Zhao to study under Zhang Wugui.

sentences.zh: 吾貴門徒甚盛，遵明伏膺數月，乃私謂其友人曰：「張生名高而義無檢格，凡所講說，不愜吾心，請更從師。

translations.literal: Wugui's disciples were very numerous; Zunming submitted to him for several months, then privately told a friend, "Master Zhang's fame is high but his conduct lacks restraint; nothing in his lectures satisfies me—I wish to find another teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Wugui had a huge following; Zunming studied under him for months, then told a friend privately, "Zhang is famous but undisciplined; his teaching does not suit me—I must change teachers."

sentences.zh: 」遂與平原田猛略就范陽孫買德受業。

translations.literal: He then went with Tian Menglue of Pingyuan to Fan Yang to study under Sun Maide.
translations.idiomatic: With Tian Menglue of Pingyuan he went to Fan Yang to study under Sun Maide.

sentences.zh: 一年，復欲去之。

translations.literal: After one year he wanted to leave again.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he wanted to move on again.

sentences.zh: 猛略謂遵明曰：「君年少從師，每不終業，千里負帙，何去就之甚。

translations.literal: Menglue said to Zunming, "You are young and every time you study with a teacher you never finish; you carry your bundles a thousand li—why do you come and go so much?"
translations.idiomatic: Menglue said, "You are still young; with each master you never finish; you haul your books a thousand li—why this constant moving?"

sentences.zh: 如此用意，終恐無成。

translations.literal: With this attitude I fear you will never succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At this rate you may never accomplish anything.

sentences.zh: 」遵明曰：「吾今始知真師所在。

translations.literal: Zunming said, "I now know where the true teacher is."
translations.idiomatic: Zunming replied, "I have finally found where the real teacher is."

sentences.zh: 」猛略曰：「何在？

translations.literal: Menglue said, "Where?"
translations.idiomatic: Menglue asked, "Where?"

sentences.zh: 」遵明乃指心曰：「正在於此。

translations.literal: Zunming pointed to his heart and said, "Right here."
translations.idiomatic: Zunming pointed to his heart: "Here."

sentences.zh: 」乃詣平原唐遷，納之，居於蠶舍。

translations.literal: He then went to Tang Qian of Pingyuan, who took him in and lodged him in a silkworm shed.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out Tang Qian of Pingyuan, who accepted him and housed him in a silkworm shed.

sentences.zh: 讀孝經、論語、毛詩、尚書、三禮，不出門院，凡經六年，時彈箏吹笛以自娛慰。

translations.literal: He read the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, Documents, and the three Ritual texts without leaving the courtyard gate; for six years in all he sometimes played zither and flute to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: For six years he never left the compound, reading Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, Documents, and the three Rituals, sometimes playing zither and flute for solace.

sentences.zh: 又知陽平館陶趙世業家有服氏春秋，是晉世永嘉舊本，遵明乃往讀之。

translations.literal: He also learned that Zhao Shiye of Guantao in Yangping had the Fu clan Spring and Autumn, an old text from the Yongjia era of Jin; Zunming went to read it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhao Shiye of Guantao in Yangping owned the Fu clan Spring and Autumn, a Jin Yongjia-era text, he went to study it.

sentences.zh: 復經數載，因手撰春秋義章，為三十卷。

translations.literal: After several more years he personally compiled Explications of the Spring and Autumn in thirty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he compiled his own Explications of the Spring and Autumn in thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 是後教授，門徒蓋寡，久之乃盛。

translations.literal: Thereafter he taught; his disciples were at first few and only after long time became many.
translations.idiomatic: When he began to teach, disciples were few; only after long years did his school flourish.

sentences.zh: 遵明每臨講坐，必持經執疏，然後敷陳，其學徒至今浸以成俗。

translations.literal: Whenever Zunming took the lecturer's seat he always held the classic and commentary in hand before expounding—a practice his students follow to this day as custom.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he lectured he held classic and commentary in hand before speaking—a habit his students still observe.

sentences.zh: 遵明講學於外二十餘年，海內莫不宗仰。

translations.literal: Zunming lectured abroad for more than twenty years; within the seas none did not look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: He taught away from home for over twenty years; all under heaven revered him.

sentences.zh: 頗好聚歛，有損儒者之風。

translations.literal: He was rather fond of amassing wealth, which marred the ru scholar's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to gather money, which sat ill with the Confucian ideal.

sentences.zh: 後廣平王懷聞而徵焉。

translations.literal: Later Prince Huai of Guangling heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Guangling later summoned him on hearing his fame.

sentences.zh: 至而尋退，不好京輦。

translations.literal: He arrived but soon withdrew, disliking the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He came but soon left, having no taste for the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，南渡河，客於任城。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang he crossed the river south and lodged in Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Xiaochang he crossed south of the river and stayed in Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 以兗州有舊，因徙居焉。

translations.literal: Because he had old ties in Yan Province he moved there to live.
translations.idiomatic: Old connections in Yan Province led him to settle there.

sentences.zh: 永安初，東道大使元羅表薦之，竟無禮辟。

translations.literal: At the start of Yong'an, Eastern Route Commissioner Yuan Luo memorialized recommending him, yet no formal appointment ever came.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an's opening year Yuan Luo as eastern commissioner recommended him, but no office was conferred.

sentences.zh: 二年，元顥入洛，任城太守李湛將舉義兵，遵明同其事。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Rencheng prefect Li Zhan was about to raise a loyal army and Zunming joined the cause.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, as Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Prefect Li Zhan of Rencheng planned to raise loyal troops and Zunming joined him.

sentences.zh: 夜至民間，為亂兵所害，時年五十五。

translations.literal: At night he went among the people and was killed by mutinous soldiers at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Going among the people by night, he was slain by disorderly troops at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，遵明弟子通直散騎常侍李業興表曰：「臣聞行道樹德，非求利於當年；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Zunming's disciple Regular Palace Attendant Li Yexing memorialized saying, "I have heard that to walk the Way and plant virtue is not to seek profit in one's own lifetime;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year two his disciple Li Yexing, regular palace attendant, memorialized: "To practice the Way and cultivate virtue is not to seek reward in life;

sentences.zh: 服義履仁，豈邀恩於沒世。

translations.literal: to embrace righteousness and tread humanity—is it to invite grace after death?
translations.idiomatic: to hold to righteousness and walk in humanity is not to court favor after death.

sentences.zh: 但天爵所存，果致式閭之禮；

translations.literal: Yet the heavenly rank one holds can indeed bring the rites of a village gate;
translations.idiomatic: Yet heaven's nobility, once possessed, may win village-gate honors;

sentences.zh: 民望攸屬，終有祠墓之榮。

translations.literal: the people's hopes resting on one can in the end bring glory of temple and tomb.
translations.idiomatic: the people's regard can at last bring ancestral shrine and tomb glory.

sentences.zh: 伏見故處士兗州徐遵明生在衡泌，弗因世族之基；

translations.literal: I humbly see that the late recluse Xu Zunming of Yan Province lived amid hidden streams, not relying on a clan foundation;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the late recluse Xu Zunming of Yan lived by quiet waters without a great clan's base;

sentences.zh: 長於原野，匪乘雕鏤之地。

translations.literal: he grew up in the open country, not riding on carved-and-inlaid ground.
translations.idiomatic: he grew in the wilds, not on inlaid floors.

sentences.zh: 而託心淵曠，置情恬雅，處靜無悶，居約不憂。

translations.literal: Yet he entrusted his heart to depth and vastness and set his feelings in quiet elegance; in stillness he knew no vexation, in simplicity he knew no worry.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed his mind on depth and openness, his spirit on calm refinement; in solitude he was untroubled, in modest living untroubled by care.

sentences.zh: 故能垂簾自精，下帷獨得，鑽經緯之微言，研聖賢之妙旨。

translations.literal: Thus he could drop the curtain and refine himself alone, lower the screen and gain understanding by himself, drilling into the subtle words of the classics and studying the wondrous purport of sages.
translations.idiomatic: Behind closed curtains he perfected himself; alone under the study screen he mastered the classics' subtlest phrases and the sages' deepest intent.

sentences.zh: 莫不入其門戶，踐其堂奧，信以稱大儒於海內，擅明師於日下矣。

translations.literal: None failed to enter his gate and tread his inner hall—truly he could be called a great ru within the seas and a luminous master under the sun.
translations.idiomatic: All who came entered his gate and inner hall; he was hailed a great Confucian under heaven and a leading teacher of the age.

sentences.zh: 是故眇眇四方，知音之類，延首慕德，跂踵依風。

translations.literal: Therefore from every distant quarter those who understood music craned their necks admiring his virtue and stood on tiptoe following his wind.
translations.idiomatic: From far corners, kindred spirits craned their necks for his virtue and stood on tiptoe in his wake.

sentences.zh: 每精廬暫闢，杖策不遠千里；

translations.literal: Whenever his humble hut briefly opened, they would not hesitate to walk a thousand li with staff in hand;
translations.idiomatic: When his study briefly opened, disciples would travel a thousand li without hesitation;

sentences.zh: 束脩受業，編錄將踰萬人。

translations.literal: presenting bundles for instruction, those who enrolled and were recorded approached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: with presentation gifts they came to study—nearly ten thousand names in the rolls.

sentences.zh: 固已企盛烈於西河，擬高蹤於北海。

translations.literal: Already he matched the great fame of Xihe and rivaled the lofty tracks of the North Sea.
translations.idiomatic: He stood beside the glory of Xihe and the lofty footsteps of the North Sea.

sentences.zh: 若慕奇好士，愛客尊賢，罷吏遊梁，紛而成列。

translations.literal: Like those who admire the unusual and honor scholars, love guests and respect the worthy, leave office and wander Liang—crowds formed in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Like the host who cherishes talent and honors guests, who leaves office to roam—students gathered in ranks.

sentences.zh: 遵明以碩德重名，首蒙禮命，曳裾雅步，眷同置醴。

translations.literal: Zunming, with his great virtue and weighty name, was first to receive ritual summons; trailing his robe with elegant step, he was favored as if wine were set out for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming, eminent in virtue and name, was first called with full ceremony; he was honored as a guest for whom wine is placed.

sentences.zh: 黃門李郁具所知明，方申薦奏之恩，處心守壑之志，潛居樂道，遂往不歸。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Yu knew him well; just as he would extend the grace of recommendation, Zunming's heart was set on guarding the ravine—he lived hidden, delighted in the Way, and went away never to return.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu of the palace staff knew him and was about to recommend him, but Zunming chose seclusion and joy in the Way and departed, never to return.

sentences.zh: 故北海王入洛之初，率土風靡，遵明確然守志，忠潔不渝，遂與太守李湛將誅叛逆。

translations.literal: Thus when the Prince of Beihai first entered Luoyang and all the land was swept along, Zunming steadfastly kept his resolve, loyal and pure without change, and together with Prefect Li Zhan planned to execute the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Beihai entered Luoyang and the realm swayed, Zunming held firm, loyal and unstained, and with Prefect Li Zhan plotted against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時有邂逅，受斃凶險。

translations.literal: By mischance he met death in peril.
translations.idiomatic: By ill chance he fell in violent death.

sentences.zh: 至誠高節，堙沒無聞，朝野人士，相與嗟悼。

translations.literal: His utmost sincerity and lofty integrity were buried unheard of; court and countryside alike mourned together.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme loyalty and high principle sank unknown; officials and commoners alike grieved.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下遠應龍序，俯執天衷，每端聽而忘昃，常坐思而候曉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, far responding to the dragon's sequence, humbly holding heaven's heart—each time you listen attentively you forget the sun's decline; often sitting in thought you wait for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, aligned with the dragon's reign and holding heaven's intent, listens until sunset is forgotten and sits in thought awaiting dawn.

sentences.zh: 雖微功小善，片言一行，莫不衣裳加室，玉帛在門。

translations.literal: Though the merit be slight and the goodness small, though the word be brief and the act alone—none fails to receive added robes and jade and silk at the door.
translations.idiomatic: Even the smallest merit, the briefest word or act, wins added robes and gifts at one's door.

sentences.zh: 況遵明冠蓋一時，師表當世，溘焉冥沒，旌紀寂寥。

translations.literal: How much more so for Zunming, who for a time topped the ranks of coaches and caps and was the model teacher of his age—suddenly he passed into darkness and his honors and record stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: All the more for Zunming, foremost in rank and example in his day—struck down in silence, his memorials left bare.

sentences.zh: 逝者長辭，無論榮價，文明敍物，敦厲斯在。

translations.literal: The departed are long gone; regardless of glory or price, to set forth civilization and order things is to encourage and strengthen what remains.
translations.idiomatic: The dead do not return; yet to order civilization and instruct the world is to exalt and inspire the living.

sentences.zh: 臣託跡諸生，親承顧眄，惟伏膺之義，感在三之重，是以越分陳愚，上諠幄座。

translations.literal: Your servant, placing himself among the students, received instruction in person; in the obligation of reverent acceptance I feel the threefold weight of grace, and so overstepping my rank I state my foolish view before the imperial curtain.
translations.idiomatic: I stand among his students and received his guidance; bound by reverence and triple obligation, I overstep rank to speak before the throne.

sentences.zh: 特乞加以顯諡，追以好爵，仰申朝廷尚德之風，下示學徒稽古之利。

translations.literal: I beg only that a shining posthumous name be added and favorable rank conferred in pursuit, so as to raise high the court's wind of honoring virtue above and show students below the profit of revering antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I ask a posthumous title and noble rank, that the court's esteem for virtue shine forth and students see the reward of classical learning.

sentences.zh: 若宸鑒昭回，曲垂矜採，則荒墳千載，式貴生平。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty's bright mirror turns and you bend pity to accept, then for a thousand years his desolate tomb will ennoble his living deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty look with favor, his humble grave will for a millennium honor his life.

sentences.zh: 」卒無贈諡。

translations.literal: In the end no posthumous gift or title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: No posthumous honors were given.

sentences.zh: 董徵，字文發，頓丘衞國人也。

translations.literal: Dong Zheng, courtesy name Wenfa, was a man of Weiguo in Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zheng, styled Wenfa, came from Weiguo in Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 祖英，高平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ying was Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Ying served as administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父虬，郡功曹。

translations.literal: His father Qiu was Merit Officer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu was commandery merit officer.

sentences.zh: 徵身長七尺二寸，好古，學尚雅素。

translations.literal: Zheng stood seven feet two inches tall, loved antiquity, and pursued learning in elegant simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet two inches, loved the ancients, and studied in refined plainness.

sentences.zh: 年十七，師清河監伯陽，受論語、毛詩、春秋、周易，就河內高望崇受周官，後於博陵劉獻之遍受諸經。

translations.literal: At seventeen he took Jian Boyang of Qinghe as teacher and received the Analects, Mao Odes, Spring and Autumn, and Book of Changes; he went to Gao Wangchong of Henei for the Offices of Zhou, and later at Liu Xianzhi of Boling he received all the classics comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he studied the Analects, Mao Odes, Spring and Autumn, and Changes under Jian Boyang of Qinghe; the Offices of Zhou under Gao Wangchong of Henei; and all classics under Liu Xianzhi of Boling.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，大義精練，講授生徒。

translations.literal: Within several years he mastered the great principles in refined detail and lectured to students.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years he mastered the classics in depth and began teaching disciples.

sentences.zh: 太和末，為四門小學博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era he became Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School.
translations.idiomatic: At Taihe's end he became erudite at the Four Gates elementary school.

sentences.zh: 後世宗詔徵入琁華宮，令孫惠蔚問以六經，仍詔徵教授京兆、清河、廣平、汝南四王，後特除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Shizong ordered Zheng into the Jade Flower Palace and had Sun Huiwei question him on the Six Classics; he also ordered Zheng to instruct the kings of Jingzhao, Qinghe, Guangling, and Runan, and later specially appointed him Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace Cadre.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong summoned him to the Jade Flower Palace for examination on the Six Classics by Sun Huiwei, had him tutor four princes, and later appointed him supernumerary palace cadre gentleman.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌之為司空、司徒，引徵為長流參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Yi of Qinghe served as Minister of Works and then Minister over the Masses, he brought Zheng in as Senior Adjutant of the Flowing Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi of Qinghe became minister of works and then minister over the masses, he took Zheng as senior adjutant.

sentences.zh: 懌遷太尉，徵為倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Yi moved to Grand Commandant, Zheng became Adjutant of the Granary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi became grand commandant, Zheng served as granary bureau adjutant.

sentences.zh: 出為沛郡太守，加揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Pei Commandery and was given the additional title General Who Raises the Array.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as administrator of Pei, with the additional rank general who raises the array.

sentences.zh: 入為太尉司馬，俄加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Minister of the Grand Commandant and soon received the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as vice minister under the grand commandant and soon gained the additional title general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以本將軍除安州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, with that general's title he was appointed Governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was made governor of An with that general's rank.

sentences.zh: 徵因述職，路次過家，置酒高會，大享邑老，乃言曰：「腰龜返國，昔人稱榮；

translations.literal: On reporting for duty Zheng passed his home on the way, set out wine for a grand gathering, and lavishly entertained the elders of his district, then said, "Returning to one's state with the turtle badge on one's belt—men of old called it glory;"
translations.idiomatic: Traveling to his post he stopped at home, feasted the district elders, and said, "To return home wearing the provincial seal was called honor of old;"

sentences.zh: 仗節還家，云胡不樂。

translations.literal: returning home bearing the staff of office—how could one not rejoice?"
translations.idiomatic: to come back with imperial credentials—why would one not rejoice?"

sentences.zh: 」因誡二三子弟曰：「此之富貴，匪自天降，乃勤學所致耳。

translations.literal: He then admonished several younger kinsmen, "This wealth and honor did not fall from heaven—it came from diligent study alone."
translations.idiomatic: He told his younger relatives, "This rank and wealth did not drop from the sky—it came from hard study alone."

sentences.zh: 」時人榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the time honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired him for this.

sentences.zh: 入為司農少卿、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of revenue and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 徵出州入卿，匪唯學業所致，亦由汝南王悅以其師資之義，為之啟請焉。

translations.literal: That Zheng moved from governorship to court minister was not due to learning alone—Prince Yue of Runan also opened the way out of respect for him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: His rise from province to court owed not only to scholarship—Prince Yue of Runan also petitioned out of respect as his former teacher.

sentences.zh: 永安初，加平東將軍，尋以老解職。

translations.literal: At the start of Yong'an he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East; soon afterward, on account of age, he resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an's opening he received general who pacifies the east; soon he retired for age.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongxi year two.

sentences.zh: 出帝以徵昔授父業，故優贈散騎常侍、都督相殷滄三州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書左僕射、相州刺史，諡曰文烈。

translations.literal: Because the Deposed Emperor's father had received instruction from Zheng, he generously posthumously granted him Regular Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Xiang, Yin, and Cang provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry with credentials equal to the Three Dukes, Left Vice Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiang, with posthumous name Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor, remembering Zheng had taught his father, posthumously made him regular palace attendant, area commander, general of chariots and cavalry with three-duke honors, left vice minister of works, and governor of Xiang, with posthumous name Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 子仲曜，武定末，儀同開府屬。

translations.literal: His son Zhongyao at the end of Wuding served as staff officer with credentials equal to a chief commandant's.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongyao at Wuding's end served on a staff with chief commandant credentials.

sentences.zh: 刁沖，字文朗，勃海饒安人也，鎮東將軍雍之曾孫。

translations.literal: Diao Chong, courtesy name Wenlang, was a man of Rao'an in Bohai, great-grandson of General Who Guards the East Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Chong, styled Wenlang, of Rao'an in Bohai, was great-grandson of General Who Guards the East Yong.

sentences.zh: 十三而孤，孝慕過人。

translations.literal: Orphaned at thirteen, his filial grief exceeded others.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at thirteen, his mourning devotion surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 其祖母司空高允女，聰明婦人也，哀其早孤，撫養尤篤。

translations.literal: His grandmother was the daughter of Minister of Works Gao Yun—a clever woman who pitied his early orphanhood and nurtured him with especial tenderness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother, daughter of Minister of Works Gao Yun, pitying his early loss, raised him with special care.

sentences.zh: 沖免喪後便志學他方，高氏泣涕留之，沖終不止。

translations.literal: After Chong left mourning he resolved to study elsewhere; the Gao clan wept and tried to keep him, but Chong would not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he wished to study away; the Gaos wept and begged him to stay, but he would not.

sentences.zh: 雖家世貴達，乃從師於外，自同諸生。

translations.literal: Although his family was noble and eminent, he went to study abroad like any ordinary student.
translations.idiomatic: Though his clan was eminent, he studied outside like any common student.

sentences.zh: 於時學制，諸生悉日直監厨，沖雖有僕隸，不令代己，身自炊爨。

translations.literal: Under the school regulations of the time all students took daily turns supervising the kitchen; though Chong had servants he would not let them replace him and cooked for himself.
translations.idiomatic: School rules required students to supervise the kitchen in rotation; Chong had servants but cooked for himself.

sentences.zh: 每師受之際，發情精專，不捨晝夜，殆忘寒暑。

translations.literal: Whenever he received instruction he gave himself with concentrated feeling, never stopping day or night, nearly forgetting cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: In study he gave himself utterly, day and night, heedless of season.

sentences.zh: 學通諸經，偏修鄭說，陰陽、圖緯、算數、天文、風氣之書莫不關綜，當世服其精博。

translations.literal: He mastered all the classics but especially cultivated the Zheng commentary tradition; books on yin-yang, charts and weft-texts, calculation, astronomy, and winds and seasons—none did he fail to integrate—and his contemporaries admired his refined breadth.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics, especially Zheng's commentaries, and also yin-yang lore, prognostic texts, mathematics, astronomy, and wind omen books—esteemed for depth and breadth.

sentences.zh: 刺史郭祚聞其盛名，訪以疑義，沖應機解辯，無不祛其久惑。

translations.literal: Governor Guo Zuo heard his great fame and visited him with doubtful points; Chong answered on the spot with disputation and never failed to dispel long-standing confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Guo Zuo sought him out with hard questions; Chong's replies always cleared old doubts.

sentences.zh: 後太守范陽盧尚之、刺史河東裴植並徵沖為功曹、[6]主簿，非所好也，受署而已，不關事務。

translations.literal: Later Administrator Lu Shangzhi of Fanyang and Governor Pei Zhi of Hedong both summoned Chong as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk—not to his taste; he accepted appointment only and did not involve himself in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Administrators Lu Shangzhi and Governor Pei Zhi summoned him as merit officer and chief clerk; he accepted titles but did not handle business.

sentences.zh: 惟以講學為心，四方學徒就其受業者歲有數百。

translations.literal: His heart was set on lecturing alone; students from the four directions who came to study under him numbered hundreds each year.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured only; hundreds of students came each year from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 沖雖儒生，而執心壯烈，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Though a Confucian scholar, Chong's resolve was bold and fierce and he did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucian by trade, he was bold and unafraid of the mighty.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，世宗舅司徒高肇擅恣威權，沖乃抗表極言其事，辭旨懇直，文義忠憤。

translations.literal: In the Yan chang era, Shizong's maternal uncle Minister over the Masses Gao Zhao arrogantly wielded power; Chong submitted a memorial forcefully stating the matter, his wording earnest and straight, his text loyal and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: During Yan chang, Gao Zhao, the emperor's uncle, abused power; Chong memorialized against him in blunt, loyal language.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌覽而歎息。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe read it and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe read it and sighed.

sentences.zh: 先是沖曾祖雍作行孝論以誡子孫，稱：「古之葬者衣之以薪，不封不樹，後世聖人易之棺椁。

translations.literal: Earlier Chong's great-grandfather Yong had written Discourse on Filial Conduct to admonish his descendants, saying, "The ancients in burial clothed the dead in firewood, neither sealing nor planting trees; later sages replaced this with coffins.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yong had written a discourse on filial conduct for his heirs: "Ancient burials used firewood wraps without mound or tree; later sages introduced coffins."

sentences.zh: 其有生則不能致養，死則厚葬過度。

translations.literal: Yet in life they cannot provide support, and in death they bury with excessive lavishness.
translations.idiomatic: In life they fail to care for parents; in death they bury with wasteful splendor.

sentences.zh: 及於末世，至蘧蒢裹尸，倮而葬者。

translations.literal: By the end age some even wrapped corpses in coarse mats and buried them naked.
translations.idiomatic: At civilization's end some wrapped bodies in rush mats and buried them bare.

sentences.zh: 確而為論，並非折衷。

translations.literal: To fix one view as dogma is in neither case the mean.
translations.idiomatic: To insist on either extreme misses the middle way.

sentences.zh: 既知二者之失豈宜同之。

translations.literal: Knowing that both err, how can one follow both alike?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing both fail, one should follow neither blindly.

sentences.zh: 當令所存者棺厚不過三寸，高不過三尺，弗用繒綵，斂以時服。

translations.literal: Let what remains use coffins no thicker than three inches and no higher than three feet, without colored silks, and shroud the body in seasonal dress.
translations.idiomatic: Coffins should be no more than three inches thick and three feet high, without brocade, the body dressed in ordinary clothes.

sentences.zh: 轜車止用白布為幔，不加畫飾，名為清素車。

translations.literal: The funeral cart should use only white cloth for its canopy, without painted ornament, and be called the Clear and Plain Cart.
translations.idiomatic: The hearse should have a white cloth canopy only, unpainted—the "clear and plain cart."

sentences.zh: 又去挽歌、方相，并盟器雜物。

translations.literal: Remove also dirge singers, exorcist figures, and assorted grave goods.
translations.idiomatic: Omit dirges, exorcist masks, and grave goods as well.

sentences.zh: 」及沖祖遵將卒，敕其子孫令奉雍遺旨。

translations.literal: When Chong's grandfather Zun was about to die he instructed his descendants to follow Yong's testament.
translations.idiomatic: When grandfather Zun lay dying he ordered descendants to obey Yong's will.

sentences.zh: 河南尹丞張普惠謂為太儉，貽書於沖叔整議其進退。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of Henan Zhang Puhui called it too spare and sent a letter to Chong's uncle Zheng to debate whether to adhere or depart.
translations.idiomatic: Henan assistant director Zhang Puhui deemed it too austere and wrote Chong's uncle Zheng to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 整令與通學議之，沖乃致書國學諸儒以論其事，學官竟不能答。

translations.literal: Zheng had fellow students discuss it; Chong then sent letters to the erudites of the National University to argue the case, and the academicians in the end could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng consulted fellow students; Chong wrote the national university scholars, who could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 沖以嫡傳祖爵東安侯。

translations.literal: Chong as eldest son inherited the ancestral marquisate of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: As eldest heir Chong inherited the marquisate of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 京兆王繼為司空也，並以高選頻辟記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Ji of Jingzhao became Minister of Works he repeatedly recruited Chong with high selection as Recorder in his secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ji of Jingzhao became minister of works he repeatedly chose Chong as secretariat recorder.

sentences.zh: 肅宗將親釋奠，於是國子助教韓神固與諸儒詣國子祭酒崔光、吏部尚書甄琛，舉其才學，奏而徵焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was about to perform the capped sacrifice in person, National University Assistant Erudite Han Shengu and the ru scholars went to Director Jingyu of the National University and Minister of Personnel Zhen Chen, commending Chong's talent and learning; they memorialized and he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: As Suzong prepared to sacrifice in person, Han Shengu and other scholars recommended Chong to Director Jingyu and Minister Zhen Chen; he was summoned on memorial.

sentences.zh: 及卒，國子博士高涼及范陽盧道侃、[7]盧景裕等復上狀陳沖業行，議奏諡曰安憲先生，祭以太牢。

translations.literal: At his death National University Erudite Gao Liang and Lu Daokan and Lu Jingyu of Fanyang again submitted statements on Chong's accomplishments and conduct, proposing posthumous title Master Anxian and sacrifice with the highest victims.
translations.idiomatic: At his death erudites Gao Liang, Lu Daokan, and Lu Jingyu memorialized for posthumous title Master Anxian and grand victim sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子欽，字志儒。

translations.literal: His son Qin, courtesy name Zhiru.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin, styled Zhiru.

sentences.zh: 早亡。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕，字仲儒，小字白頭，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jingyu, courtesy name Zhongru, childhood name Whitehead, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingyu, styled Zhongru, nicknamed Whitehead, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 章武伯同之兄子。

translations.literal: He was the son of the elder brother of Marquis of Zhangwu Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He was nephew of Marquis of Zhangwu Tong.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，專經為學。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and keen, dedicating himself to classic learning.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, he devoted himself to the classics.

sentences.zh: 居拒馬河，將一老婢作食，妻子不自隨從。

translations.literal: Living on the Juma River he had only one old maidservant prepare food; wife and children did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Juma River one old servant cooked for him; his family did not live with him.

sentences.zh: 又避地大寧山，不營世事，居無所業，惟在注解。

translations.literal: He also fled to Mount Daning to escape turmoil, did not pursue worldly affairs, had no other occupation save commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing chaos on Mount Daning, he shunned affairs and did nothing but write commentaries.

sentences.zh: 其叔父同職居顯要，而景裕止於園舍，情均郊野，謙恭守道，貞素自得。

translations.literal: His uncle Tong held prominent office while Jingyu stayed in a garden lodge, his feelings equal to the open fields, humble and observant of the Way, chaste and self-content.
translations.idiomatic: While uncle Tong held high office, Jingyu lived in a garden cottage, plain as the countryside, humble and content on the Way.

sentences.zh: 由是世號居士。

translations.literal: For this the age called him Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Hence men called him the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，除國子博士，參議正聲，甚見親遇，待以不臣之禮。

translations.literal: At the start of the Former Deposed Emperor he was appointed Erudite of the National University to discuss correcting the pitch standard and was greatly favored, treated with the etiquette due a non-subject.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former deposed emperor he became national university erudite to help fix the pitch pipes, favored and treated almost as an equal.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，以例解。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongxi he was dismissed under the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongxi's opening he left office under routine.

sentences.zh: 天平中，還鄉里，與邢子才、魏季景、魏收、邢昕等同徵赴鄴。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he returned to his home district and, with Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin, was jointly summoned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he went home, then with Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin was summoned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 景裕寓託僧寺，講聽不已。

translations.literal: Jingyu lodged at a Buddhist monastery and never stopped lecturing and listening.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed at a monastery and never ceased teaching and listening.

sentences.zh: 未幾，歸本郡。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 河間邢摩納與景裕從兄仲禮據鄉作逆，逼其同反，以應元寶炬。

translations.literal: Xing Monuo of Hejian and Jingyu's cousin Zhongli held the district in rebellion and forced them to join, in response to Yuan Baoju.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Monuo of Hejian and cousin Zhongli rebelled locally and forced Jingyu's circle to join Yuan Baoju.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王命都督賀拔仁討平之。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi ordered Area Commander Heba Ren to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi sent Heba Ren to put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 聞景裕經明行著，驛馬特徵，既而舍之，使教諸子。

translations.literal: Hearing that Jingyu's classics were clear and his conduct outstanding, he sent a post horse to summon him specially; soon he released him and had him teach the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Jingyu was eminent in learning and conduct, he summoned him by post horse, then set him to teach the princes.

sentences.zh: 在館十日一歸家，隨以鼎食。

translations.literal: In the lodge he returned home once every ten days, with full meals sent after him.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days in the princes' household he went home, attended with rich food.

sentences.zh: 景裕風儀言行，雅見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Jingyu's bearing, speech, and conduct were much admired in elegant praise.
translations.idiomatic: His manner and speech won elegant praise.

sentences.zh: 先是景裕注周易、尚書、孝經、論語、禮記、老子，其毛詩、春秋左氏未訖。

translations.literal: Previously Jingyu had commented on the Changes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Record of Ritual, and Laozi; his Mao Odes and Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn were unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: He had commented on the Changes, Documents, Filial Piety, Analects, Record of Ritual, and Laozi; Mao Odes and Zuo Commentary remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王入相，於第開講，招延時儁，令景裕解所注易。

translations.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi entered the chancellorship he opened lectures at his residence, gathered leading men of the time, and had Jingyu expound his commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang became chancellor he lectured at home, gathered talent, and had Jingyu explain his Changes commentary.

sentences.zh: 景裕理義精微，吐發閑雅。

translations.literal: Jingyu's reasoning was subtle and his delivery leisurely and refined.
translations.idiomatic: His reasoning was fine and his speech calm and polished.

sentences.zh: 時有問難，或相詆訶，大聲厲色，言至不遜，而景裕神彩儼然，風調如一，從容往復，無際可尋。

translations.literal: When there were questions and challenges, some reviled him with loud voices and harsh color, speech reaching insolence—yet Jingyu's spirit remained composed and his tone uniform, responding at ease with no gap to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: Some challengers shouted abuse, yet Jingyu stayed serene and answered without opening.

sentences.zh: 由是士君子嗟美之。

translations.literal: For this gentlemen sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，元顥入洛，[8]以為中書郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jingyu was appointed Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he was made palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，復除國子博士。

translations.literal: At the start of Putai he was again appointed Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At Putai's opening he again became national university erudite.

sentences.zh: 進退其間，未曾有得失之色。

translations.literal: Between advancement and withdrawal he never showed color of gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: Through promotion and demotion his face never changed.

sentences.zh: 性清靜，淡於榮利，弊衣粗食，恬然自安，終日端嚴，如對賓客。

translations.literal: By nature he was clear and still, indifferent to glory and profit, in worn clothes and coarse food, tranquil and self-assured, all day upright as if facing guests.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and quiet by nature, indifferent to rank, in patched clothes and plain food, always dignified as before guests.

sentences.zh: 興和中，補齊王開府屬，卒於晉陽，齊獻武王悼惜之。

translations.literal: In Xinghe he was appointed staff officer to Prince Qi and died at Jinyang; Prince Xianwu of Qi mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe he served Prince Qi as staff officer and died at Jinyang; Prince Xianwu grieved.

sentences.zh: 景裕雖不聚徒教授，所注易大行於世。

translations.literal: Though Jingyu did not gather disciples to teach, his commentary on the Changes spread widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not maintain a school, his Changes commentary circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 又好釋氏，通其大義。

translations.literal: He also favored Buddhism and grasped its great principles.
translations.idiomatic: He also favored Buddhism and understood its core teachings.

sentences.zh: 天竺胡沙門道悕每論諸經論，輒託景裕為之序。

translations.literal: The Indian monk Daoxi, whenever he discussed sutras and treatises, always entrusted Jingyu to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: The Indian monk Daoxi always asked Jingyu to preface his sutra discussions.

sentences.zh: 景裕之敗也。

translations.literal: When Jingyu met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyu fell into trouble.

sentences.zh: 繫晉陽獄，至心誦經，枷鎖自脫。

translations.literal: Imprisoned in Jinyang, he recited sutras with utmost sincerity and the cangue and fetters fell away by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned at Jinyang, he chanted sutras devoutly and his shackles fell off.

sentences.zh: 是時又有人負罪當死，夢沙門教講經，覺時如所夢，默誦千遍，臨刑刀折，主者以聞，赦之。

translations.literal: At that time another man guilty of capital crime dreamed a monk taught him to recite a sutra; waking he did as in the dream and silently recited a thousand times; at execution the blade broke; the officer reported it and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Another condemned man dreamed a monk taught him a sutra; he recited it a thousand times; at execution the blade broke and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 此經遂行於世，號曰高王觀世音。

translations.literal: This sutra then spread in the world and was called the High King's Avalokitesvara.
translations.idiomatic: That sutra spread as the High King Avalokitesvara Sutra.

sentences.zh: 李同軌，趙郡高邑人，陽夏太守義深之弟。

translations.literal: Li Tonggui was a man of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery, younger brother of Yaci, Administrator of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tonggui of Gaoyi in Zhao was younger brother of Yangxia administrator Yaci.

sentences.zh: 體貌魁岸，腰帶十圍，學綜諸經，多所治誦，兼讀釋氏，又好醫術。

translations.literal: Of imposing build, his belt ten spans round, he synthesized all classics and recited many; he also read Buddhism and loved medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Imposing in build, with a ten-span waist, he mastered many classics, read Buddhist texts, and studied medicine.

sentences.zh: 年二十二，舉秀才，射策，除奉朝請，領國子助教。

translations.literal: At twenty-two he was nominated as Presented Scholar, passed the archery-and-writing examination, was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and concurrent Assistant Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-two he passed the presented scholar examination, became court gentleman for attendance and national university assistant erudite.

sentences.zh: 轉著作郎，典儀注，修國史，遷國子博士，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He moved to Compiler, managed ritual protocols, edited the national history, was promoted to Erudite of the National University, and given the additional title General Who Subdues Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He became compiler, handled ritual codes, edited national history, rose to national university erudite, and received general who subdues barbarians.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，出帝幸平等寺，僧徒講法，敕同軌論難，音韻閑朗，往復可觀，出帝善之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi the Deposed Emperor visited Pingdeng Temple where monks lectured the Dharma; he ordered Tonggui to debate; his tone was leisurely and clear and the exchange was worth viewing; the emperor was pleased.
