translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year two the deposed emperor visited Pingdeng Temple for dharma debate and ordered Tonggui to argue; his voice was clear and the exchange pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三年春，釋菜，詔延公卿學官於顯陽殿，敕祭酒劉廞講孝經，黃門李郁講禮記，中書舍人盧景宣解大戴禮夏小正篇。

translations.literal: In the third year spring, at the capped sacrifice, an edict extended dukes, ministers, and academicians to the Xianyang Hall; the Director of the National University Liu Yan was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Palace Attendant Li Yu on the Record of Ritual, and Palace Secretariat Draftsman Lu Jingxuan to expound the Summer Offices chapter from the Elder Dai Record of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year three, at the capped sacrifice, officials and scholars gathered at Xianyang Hall; Liu Yan lectured on Filial Piety, Li Yu on the Record of Ritual, and Lu Jingxuan on the Elder Dai Summer Offices.

sentences.zh: 時廣招儒學，引令預聽。

translations.literal: At the time many Confucian scholars were recruited and invited to listen in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Many scholars were summoned to attend.

sentences.zh: 同軌經義素優，辯析兼美，而不得執經，深為慨恨。

translations.literal: Tonggui's mastery of classic meaning had long been superior and his analysis and exposition were both fine, yet he could not hold the classic in lecture—a deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui excelled in doctrine and debate yet could not lead the classic lecture—to his lasting regret.

sentences.zh: 天平中，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he became vice director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 興和中，兼通直散騎常侍，使蕭衍。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he was concurrently Regular Palace Attendant and envoy to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe he also served as regular palace attendant and envoy to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍深耽釋學，遂集名僧於其愛敬、同泰二寺，講𣵀盤大品經，引同軌預席。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan was deeply devoted to Buddhist learning and gathered eminent monks at his Ai'jing and Tongtai monasteries to lecture on the Nirvana Mahayana sutra, inviting Tonggui to take a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in Buddhist study, Xiao Yan gathered monks at Ai'jing and Tongtai to expound the Nirvana Sutra and seated Tonggui among them.

sentences.zh: 衍兼遣其朝臣並共觀聽。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan also sent his court ministers together to observe and listen.
translations.idiomatic: He also had his ministers attend.

sentences.zh: 同軌論難久之，道俗咸以為善。

translations.literal: Tonggui debated at length and clergy and laity alike deemed it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui debated long; monks and laymen alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕卒，齊獻武王引同軌在館教諸公子，甚加禮之。

translations.literal: When Lu Jingyu died, Prince Xianwu of Qi brought Tonggui into the lodge to teach the princes and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Jingyu's death, Prince Xianwu had Tonggui teach the princes in the lodge with high honor.

sentences.zh: 每旦入授，日暮始歸。

translations.literal: Each morning he entered to instruct and only returned at day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he taught from morning until evening.

sentences.zh: 緇素請業者，同軌夜為說解，四時恒爾，不以為倦。

translations.literal: Monks and laymen who sought instruction—Tonggui explained for them at night, four seasons without change, never weary of it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought teaching he instructed at night as well, year round, never weary.

sentences.zh: 武定四年夏卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding, summer, he died at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in summer, Wuding year four, at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 時人傷惜之，齊獻武王亦殊嗟悼，贈襚甚厚。

translations.literal: Men of the time grieved; Prince Xianwu of Qi also mourned deeply and granted lavish funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mourned him; Prince Xianwu grieved and gave rich funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、瀛州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Ying, with posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was general of agile cavalry and governor of Ying, posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 李業興，上黨長子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yexing was a man of Changzi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing came from Changzi in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 祖虬，父玄紀，並以儒學舉孝廉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiu and father Xuanji both entered office as Filial and Incorrupt through Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Qiu and father Xuanji both became filial-and-incorrupt through Confucian study.

sentences.zh: 玄紀卒於金鄉令。

translations.literal: Xuanji died while Magistrate of Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanji died as magistrate of Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 業興少耿介，志學精力，負帙從師，不憚勤苦。

translations.literal: Yexing from youth was upright and resolute, devoted his will to learning with full energy, carried bundles and followed teachers, unafraid of toil.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was stubborn and studious, bearing books to teachers without flinching from hardship.

sentences.zh: 耽思章句，好覽異說。

translations.literal: He pondered deeply chapter and phrase and loved reading unusual theories.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded over lines and clauses and loved unorthodox texts.

sentences.zh: 晚乃師事徐遵明於趙魏之間。

translations.literal: Only later did he take Xu Zunming as teacher between Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he study under Xu Zunming in Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 時有漁陽鮮于靈馥亦聚徒教授，而遵明聲譽未高，著錄尚寡。

translations.literal: At the time Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang also gathered disciples to teach, while Zunming's fame was not yet high and those on his register were still few.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang also taught, while Zunming's fame was still modest and his roster small.

sentences.zh: 業興乃詣靈馥黌舍，類受業者。

translations.literal: Yexing then went to Lingfu's school, resembling those receiving instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing went to Lingfu's school posing as a student.

sentences.zh: 靈馥乃謂曰：「李生久逐羌博士，何所得也？

translations.literal: Lingfu then said to him, "Master Li has long chased the Qiang doctor—what have you gained?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu said, "You have long run after that Qiang master—what have you learned?"

sentences.zh: 」業興默爾不言。

translations.literal: Yexing silently said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 及靈馥說左傳，業興問其大義數條，靈馥不能對。

translations.literal: When Lingfu expounded the Zuo Commentary, Yexing asked several points of its great meaning and Lingfu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingfu lectured on the Zuo Commentary, Yexing asked major points Lingfu could not answer.

sentences.zh: 於是振衣而起曰：「羌弟子正如此耳！

translations.literal: Thereupon he shook out his robes, rose, and said, "A Qiang disciple is just like this!"
translations.idiomatic: He shook his robe, stood, and said, "So much for a Qiang master's pupil!"

sentences.zh: 」遂便徑還。

translations.literal: He then went straight back.
translations.idiomatic: And went straight home.

sentences.zh: 自此靈馥生徒傾學而就遵明。

translations.literal: From this Lingfu's students all shifted study to go to Zunming.
translations.idiomatic: After that Lingfu's students flocked to Zunming.

sentences.zh: 遵明學徒大盛，業興之為也。

translations.literal: Zunming's disciples greatly flourished—it was Yexing who brought it about.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming's school swelled—thanks to Yexing.

sentences.zh: 後乃博涉百家，圖緯、風角、天文、占候無不詳練，尤長算歷。

translations.literal: Later he broadly covered the hundred schools; charts and weft-texts, wind horns, astronomy, and divination by omens—none was he not versed in—and he was especially expert in calculation and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: Later he mastered the hundred schools, prognostics, wind omens, astronomy, and divination, especially calendrics.

sentences.zh: 雖在貧賤，常自矜負，若禮待不足，縱於權貴，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Though poor and lowly he often prided himself; if ritual treatment fell short, even toward the powerful he would not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor he held himself high; insufficient courtesy from the mighty he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 後為王遵業門客。

translations.literal: Later he became a client of Wang Zunye.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Wang Zunye as client.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為校書郎。

translations.literal: Nominated Filial and Incorrupt, he became Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he became collator.

sentences.zh: 以世行趙𢾺曆，節氣後辰下算，延昌中，業興乃為戊子元曆上之。

translations.literal: Because the age used the Zhao Xian calendar with solar terms lagging and calculations falling behind, in Yan chang Yexing submitted the Wuzi Origin Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The reign used the Zhao Xian calendar with drifting solar terms; in Yan chang Yexing submitted the Wuzi Origin Calendar.

sentences.zh: 於時屯騎校尉張洪、盪寇將軍張龍祥等九家各獻新曆，世宗詔令共為一曆。

translations.literal: At the time Colonel of the Retainers Zhang Hong, General Who Sweeps Bandits Zhang Longxiang, and nine households each presented new calendars; Emperor Shizong ordered them combined into one calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Nine scholars including Zhang Hong and Zhang Longxiang each offered new calendars; Shizong ordered one unified calendar.

sentences.zh: 洪等後遂共推業興為主，成戊子曆，[9]正光三年奏行之。

translations.literal: Hong and the others afterward jointly pushed Yexing as lead and completed the Wuzi calendar; in the third year of Zheng guang it was memorialized and put into use.
translations.idiomatic: They made Yexing lead author of the Wuzi calendar, enacted in Zheng guang year three.

sentences.zh: 事在律曆志。

translations.literal: The matter is in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and Calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded in the treatise on pitch pipes and calendars.

sentences.zh: 累遷奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to court gentleman for attendance.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧征蠻，引為騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu of Linhuai campaigned against the Man tribes he brought Yexing in as Cavalry Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Linhuai took him as cavalry adjutant on a southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 後廣陵王淵北征，復為外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Later when Prince Yuan of Guangling marched north he again served as Outer Corps Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuan of Guangling marched north he again served as outer corps adjutant.

sentences.zh: 業興以殷曆甲寅，黃帝辛卯，徒有積元，術數亡缺，業興又修之，各為一卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: Yexing held that the Yin calendar's jia-yin and Yellow Emperor's xin-mao had accumulated origins in name only while numerology was missing; Yexing repaired each in one fascicle, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He revised deficient Yin-era calendar tables in two fascicles that circulated.

sentences.zh: 建義初，敕典儀注，未幾除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyi he was ordered to manage ritual protocols; before long he was appointed Assistant Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyi's start he managed ritual codes; soon he became assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，以前造曆之勳，賜爵長子伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, for earlier service on the calendar, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an year two he received the barony of Changzi for calendar work.

sentences.zh: 遭憂解任，尋起復本官。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning but soon was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for mourning but soon returned to office.

sentences.zh: 元曄之竊號也，除通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye usurped the title Yexing was appointed Regular Vice Director of the Palace Cadre.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye seized the throne he became regular vice director of the palace cadre.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，沙汰侍官，業興仍在通直，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai, when attendant officials were purged, Yexing remained in the regular cadre with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai year one, after an attendant purge, he kept his post with general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 又除征虜將軍、中散大夫，仍在通直。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Conquers Barbarians and Palace Counsellor, still in the regular cadre.
translations.idiomatic: He also became general who conquers barbarians and palace counsellor, still in the regular cadre.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，轉散騎侍郎，仍以典儀之勤，特賞一階，除平東將軍、光祿大夫，尋加安西將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Taichang he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Cadre; for service managing rituals he was specially rewarded one rank, appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and soon given the additional General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang he became vice director of the palace cadre, gained a rank for ritual service, and received eastern and western general titles.

sentences.zh: 後以出帝登極之初，預行禮事，封屯留縣開國子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Later, because at the start of the Deposed Emperor's accession he took part in ritual affairs, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Tunliu with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping at the deposed emperor's accession rites he received the viscounty of Tunliu, five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉中軍將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Central Army and Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of the central army and regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年二月，出帝釋奠，業興與魏季景、溫子昇、竇瑗為摘句。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Yongxi the Deposed Emperor performed the capped sacrifice; Yexing with Wei Jijing, Wen Zisheng, and Dou Yuan selected passages.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year three, month two, at the capped sacrifice Yexing, Wei Jijing, Wen Zisheng, and Dou Yuan chose texts.

sentences.zh: 後入為侍讀。

translations.literal: Later he entered as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He later became lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴之始，起部郎中辛術奏曰：「今皇居徙御，百度創始，營構一興，必宜中制。

translations.literal: At the start of the move to Ye, Director of Construction Xin Shu memorialized saying, "Now the imperial residence shifts and all standards are newly founded; once construction rises it must fit the central model.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Ye, Director of Construction Xin Shu memorialized that new capital building must follow central norms.

sentences.zh: 上則憲章前代，下則模寫洛京。

translations.literal: Above it should take the statutes of former ages as charter; below it should model Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It should follow former dynasties above and Luoyang below.

sentences.zh: 今鄴都雖舊，基址毀滅，又圖記參差，事宜審定。

translations.literal: Though Ye was an old capital its foundations are ruined and the maps and records disagree—affairs need careful fixing.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's foundations were ruined and maps conflicted—matters needed fixing.

sentences.zh: 臣雖曰職司，學不稽古，國家大事非敢專之。

translations.literal: Your servant's office is such yet his learning does not examine antiquity; he dare not monopolize a state great matter.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not decide alone a matter of state.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍李業興碩學通儒，博聞多識，萬門千戶，所宜訪詢。

translations.literal: Regular Palace Attendant Li Yexing is a leading scholar and comprehensive ru, broad in hearing and rich in knowledge—for the myriad gates and thousand households he is the one who should be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing, regular palace attendant, should be consulted—a master of wide learning.

sentences.zh: 今求就之披圖案記，考定是非，參古雜今，折中為制，召畫工并所須調度，具造新圖，申奏取定。

translations.literal: I now ask to go to him to spread out maps and records, examine and fix right and wrong, mix ancient with present, and strike the mean as standard; summon painters and all needed supplies, fully make new maps, and memorialized for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Let him compare maps old and new, settle disputes, and draft approved plans with painters.

sentences.zh: 庶經始之日，執事無疑。

translations.literal: Then on the day construction begins those in charge will have no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Then builders will act without doubt.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，除鎮南將軍，尋為侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was appointed General Who Guards the South; soon he became Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year two he became general who guards the south, then lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 於時尚書右僕射、營構大將高隆之被詔繕治三署樂器、衣服及百戲之屬，乃奏請業興共參其事。

translations.literal: At the time Right Vice Minister of Works and General of Grand Construction Gao Longzhi received an edict to repair the three offices' musical instruments, garments, and the hundred entertainments; he memorialized asking Yexing jointly to take part.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi, repairing palace music and regalia, asked Yexing to assist.

sentences.zh: 四年，與兼散騎常侍李諧、[10]兼吏部郎盧元明使蕭衍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with Concurrent Regular Palace Attendant Li Xie and Concurrent Director of Personnel Lu Yuanming he was envoy to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he went as envoy to Xiao Yan with Li Xie and Lu Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 衍散騎常侍朱异問業興曰：「魏洛中委粟山是南郊邪？

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Regular Palace Attendant Zhu Yi asked Yexing, "Is Mount Weisu in Luoyang the southern suburb?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi asked whether Mount Weisu near Luoyang was the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「委粟是圓丘，非南郊。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "Weisu is the Round Mound, not the southern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said Weisu was the round mound altar, not the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「北間郊、丘異所，是用鄭義。

translations.literal: Yi said, "In the north suburb and mound are separate places—therefore the Zheng interpretation is used.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said the north used Zheng's separate altar reading.

sentences.zh: 我此中用王義。

translations.literal: Here we use the Wang interpretation."
translations.idiomatic: In Liang they used Wang's reading."

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「然，洛京郊、丘之處專用鄭解。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "So—in Luoyang the places of suburb and mound rely solely on Zheng's explanation."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said Luoyang ritual sites followed Zheng alone.

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「若然，女子逆降傍親亦從鄭以不？

translations.literal: Yi said, "If so, for a woman descending in mourning to collateral kin does one also follow Zheng or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked whether women's mourning for collateral kin also followed Zheng.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「此之一事，亦不專從。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "On this one matter one also does not follow exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said not exclusively on that either.

sentences.zh: 若卿此間用王義，除禫應用二十五月，何以王儉喪禮禫用二十七月也？

translations.literal: If your side here uses Wang's meaning, after the mourning period end-of-mourning should use twenty-five months—why did Wang Jian's mourning rites use twenty-seven months for end-of-mourning?"
translations.idiomatic: If Liang used Wang, why did Wang Jian's rites use twenty-seven months for end of mourning?"

sentences.zh: 」异遂不答。

translations.literal: Yi then did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had no reply.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「我昨見明堂四柱方屋，都無五九之室，當是裴頠所制。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall with four pillars and a square roof, entirely without five-by-nine chambers—it must be Pei Ji's design.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the Bright Hall's square roof lacked five-by-nine chambers—Pei Ji's design.

sentences.zh: 明堂上圓下方，裴唯除室耳。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The classic Bright Hall is round above, square below; Pei removed inner chambers only.

sentences.zh: 今此上不圓何也？

translations.literal: This one is not round above—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Why is yours not round on top?"

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「圓方之說，經典無文，何怪於方？

translations.literal: Yi said, "The round-and-square theory has no text in the classics—why wonder at square?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said classics never specify round and square—why object to square?"

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「圓方之言，出處甚明，卿自不見。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "The round-and-square statement has a very clear source—you yourself do not see it.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the round-square doctrine is well attested—Yi had not seen it.

sentences.zh: 見卿錄梁主孝經義亦云上圓下方，卿言豈非自相矛盾！

translations.literal: I see in your collected Liang ruler's Meaning of the Filial Classic it also says round above and square below—are your words not self-contradictory!"
translations.idiomatic: Your own Filial Classic commentary says round above, square below—you contradict yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「若然，圓方竟出何經？

translations.literal: Yi said, "If so, from which classic does round-and-square ultimately come?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked which classic taught round and square.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「出孝經援神契。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "It comes from the Filial Classic's Apocryphal Divine Covenant."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cited the Filial Classic apocryphon Divine Covenant.

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「緯候之書，何用信也！

translations.literal: Yi said, "Apocryphal prognostic books—why trust them!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi dismissed weft-text apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「卿若不信，靈威仰、叶光紀之類經典亦無出者，卿復信不？

translations.literal: Yexing said, "If you do not trust them, for things like Lingwei Yang and Yeguang Ji the classics also have no source—do you trust those or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Yexing asked whether he also rejected omen texts with no canonical source.

sentences.zh: 」异不答。

translations.literal: Yi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was silent.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍親問業興曰：「聞卿善於經義，儒、玄之中何所通達？

translations.literal: Xiao Yan personally asked Yexing, "I hear you are good at classic meaning—between Confucian and Dark Learning what do you penetrate?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan asked what he mastered among Confucian and Dark Learning.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「少為書生，止讀五典，至於深義，不辨通釋。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "In youth I was a book student and read only the Five Classics; as for deep meaning I cannot distinguish comprehensive explanation."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said he had read only the Five Classics and could not claim deep mastery.

sentences.zh: 」衍問：「詩周南，王者之風，繫之周公；

translations.literal: Yan asked, "In the Odes, Zhou Nan is the wind of the king and is attached to the Duke of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked why Zhou Nan, the king's wind, was tied to the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 邵南，仁賢之風，繫之邵公。

translations.literal: Shao Nan is the wind of the humane and worthy and is attached to the Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Nan, wind of the worthy, to the Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 何名為繫？

translations.literal: Why is it called 'attached'?"
translations.idiomatic: What does 'attached' mean?"

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「鄭注儀禮云：昔大王、王季居于岐陽，躬行邵南之教，以興王業。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "Zheng's note on the Ceremonies says: Formerly King Da and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally practiced Shao Nan's teaching to raise the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cited Zheng on the Ceremonies: King Da and King Ji at Qiyang taught Shao Nan to build the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及文王行今周南之教以受命。

translations.literal: When King Wen practiced today's Zhou Nan teaching he received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen then taught Zhou Nan and received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 作邑於酆，分其故地，屬之二公。

translations.literal: Making a capital at Feng, he divided the former lands and assigned them to the two dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At Feng he divided the old domain between the two dukes.

sentences.zh: 名為繫。

translations.literal: This is called 'attached.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hence 'attached.'"

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「若是故地，應自統攝，何由分封二公？

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "If it was the former lands they should have been under unified rule—how could they be enfeoffed to two dukes?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked why enfeoffment was needed if the land was already his.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「文王為諸侯之時所化之本國，今既登九五之尊，不可復守諸侯之地，故分封二公。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "It was the homeland transformed while Wen was still a feudal lord; now that he has ascended to the nine-five position he cannot again hold a feudal lord's lands, and so he enfeoffed the two dukes."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said as emperor Wen could no longer hold a feudal domain, so he enfeoffed the two dukes.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「乾卦初稱『潛龍』，二稱『見龍』，至五『飛龍』。

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "In the Qian hexagram at first it says 'hidden dragon,' at second 'dragon appears,' and at fifth 'flying dragon.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked about the Qian hexagram's hidden, appearing, and flying dragon.

sentences.zh: 初可名為虎。

translations.literal: At first could it be called tiger?
translations.idiomatic: At first could it be called tiger?

sentences.zh: 」問意小乖。

translations.literal: The intent of the question was slightly off.
translations.idiomatic: The question was slightly skewed.

sentences.zh: 業興對：「學識膚淺，不足仰酬。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "Learning shallow and skin-deep, not enough to repay looking up."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing demurred that his learning was too shallow.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「尚書『正月上日受終文祖』，此是何正？

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "In the Documents 'on the first day of the first month he received the end at Wen the Ancestor'—what first month is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked which 'first month' the Documents meant at Wen the Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「此是夏正月。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "This is the Xia first month."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said the Xia calendar's first month.

sentences.zh: 」衍言何以得知。

translations.literal: Yan said how does one know this.
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked how he knew.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「案尚書中候運行篇云『日月營始』，故知夏正。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "According to the Running Phases section of the Documents Apocryphon it says 'sun and moon begin their circuit'—hence one knows it is the Xia first month."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cited the Documents apocryphon Running Phases: 'sun and moon begin their circuit'—therefore the Xia first month.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「堯時以何月為正？

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "In Yao's time which month was taken as first?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked which month Yao used as new year.

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「自堯以上，書典不載，實所不知。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "From Yao upward the written canons do not record it—I truly do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said records before Yao do not say; he did not know.

sentences.zh: 」衍又云：「『寅賓出日』，即是正月。

translations.literal: Yan again said, "'Guest the rising sun at yin' is itself the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said 'guest the rising sun at yin' is the first month.

sentences.zh: 『日中星鳥，以殷仲春』，即是二月。

translations.literal: 'At midday the star Bird, marking the mid-spring of Yin' is itself the second month.
translations.idiomatic: 'Midday, the Bird star, Yin mid-spring' is the second month.

sentences.zh: 此出堯典，何得云堯時不知用何正也？

translations.literal: This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can one say that in Yao's time one did not know which first month was used?"
translations.idiomatic: This is from the Canon of Yao—how can Yao not have known his calendar?"

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「雖三正不同，言時節者皆據夏時正月。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "Though the three first months differ, when speaking of seasons all rely on the first month of Xia time.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said though the three calendars differ, seasonal statements use Xia's first month.

sentences.zh: 周禮，仲春二月會男女之無夫家者。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, in the second month of mid-spring they gather men and women without spouses.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou gathers unmarried men and women in mid-spring's second month.

sentences.zh: 雖自周書，月亦夏時。

translations.literal: Though from a Zhou book, the month is still Xia time.
translations.idiomatic: Though a Zhou text, the month is Xia reckoning.

sentences.zh: 堯之日月，亦當如此。

translations.literal: Yao's sun and moon should likewise be so.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's calendar should be the same.

sentences.zh: 但所見不深，無以辨析明問。

translations.literal: Only what I have seen is not deep—I have no means to analyze and clarify the question.
translations.idiomatic: My reading is too shallow to answer clearly.

sentences.zh: 」衍又曰：「禮，原壤之母死，孔子助其沐椁。

translations.literal: Yan again said, "In the Ritual, when Yuanrang's mother died, Confucius helped with washing and coffin boards.
translations.idiomatic: Yan cited Yuanrang's mother's funeral and Confucius helping with the coffin.

sentences.zh: 原壤叩木而歌曰：『久矣夫，予之不託於音也。

translations.literal: Yuanrang knocked wood and sang, 'Long has it been since I was not entrusted to music.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrang tapped wood and sang that he had long been without music.

sentences.zh: [11]狸首之班然，執女手之卷然。

translations.literal: [11] The otter-head pattern orderly, holding your hand coiled.
translations.idiomatic: [11] 'The otter-head pattern spread fair; I hold your coiled hand.'

sentences.zh: 』孔子聖人，而與原壤為友？

translations.literal: Confucius is a sage—yet he befriended Yuanrang?"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius was a sage—yet befriended Yuanrang?"

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「孔子即自解，言親者不失其為親，故者不失其為故。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "Confucius himself explained, saying that kin should not cease to be kin and old ties should not cease to be old ties."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said Confucius explained that kin remain kin and old ties remain old ties.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「原壤何處人？

translations.literal: He again asked, "What place was Yuanrang from?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked where Yuanrang was from.

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「鄭注云：原壤，孔子幼少之舊。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "Zheng's note says Yuanrang was Confucius's friend from early youth—therefore he was a man of Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing cited Zheng: Yuanrang was Confucius's childhood friend—thus from Lu.

sentences.zh: 故是魯人。

translations.literal: Therefore he was a man of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: So he was a Lu man.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「孔子聖人，所存必可法。

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "Confucius is a sage; what he preserved must be followable.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said a sage's conduct must be exemplary.

sentences.zh: 原壤不孝，有逆人倫，何以存故舊之小節，廢不孝之大罪？

translations.literal: Yuanrang was unfilial and violated human relations—why preserve the small courtesy of old friendship and abandon the great crime of unfiliality?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrang was unfilial—why keep an old friendship and ignore that great fault?"

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「原壤所行，事自彰著。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "Yuanrang's conduct was manifest in the affairs themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said Yuanrang's conduct spoke for itself.

sentences.zh: 幼少之交，非是今始，既無大故，何容棄之？

translations.literal: The friendship of early youth was not begun only now; since there was no great breach, how could one cast him off?"
translations.idiomatic: Their childhood tie was long-standing; without grave cause, why abandon him?"

sentences.zh: 孔子深敦故舊之義，於理無失。

translations.literal: Confucius deeply honored the meaning of old ties—in principle he did not err."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius deeply honored old friendship—rightly so."

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「孔子聖人，何以書原壤之事，垂法萬代？

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "Confucius is a sage—why record Yuanrang's affair and hand down a law for ten thousand generations?"
translations.idiomatic: Why record Yuanrang for all posterity?"

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「此是後人所錄，非孔子自制。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "This was recorded by later men, not composed by Confucius himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said later hands recorded it, not Confucius himself.

sentences.zh: 猶合葬於防，如此之類，禮記之中動有百數。

translations.literal: Like joint burial at Fang—such cases in the Record of Ritual number in the hundreds."
translations.idiomatic: Like joint burial at Fang—hundreds of such cases in the Record of Ritual."

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「易曰太極，是有無？

translations.literal: Yan again asked, "The Changes speaks of the Supreme Pole—is it being or non-being?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked whether the Supreme Pole was being or non-being.

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「所傳太極是有，素不玄學，何敢輒酬。」

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "The transmitted Supreme Pole is being; I have never studied Dark Learning—how dare I answer rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said tradition treats the Pole as being; he dared not dabble in Dark Learning.

sentences.zh: 業興愛好墳籍，鳩集不已，手自補治，躬加題帖，其家所有，垂將萬卷。

translations.literal: Yexing loved and collected books, gathering without cease; he personally repaired them and added title slips himself—the family's holdings approached ten thousand fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He collected books endlessly, mended and labeled them himself—nearly ten thousand volumes at home.

sentences.zh: 覽讀不息，多有異聞，諸儒服其淵博。

translations.literal: He read without rest and had much unusual knowledge; the ru scholars admired his depth and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Reading ceaselessly he amassed rare learning; scholars admired his breadth.

sentences.zh: 性豪俠，重意氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and chivalrous and valued spirit and honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was chivalrous and valued loyalty.

sentences.zh: 人有急難，委之歸命，便能容匿。

translations.literal: When men were in urgent trouble they entrusted themselves to him for refuge and he could shelter and hide them.
translations.idiomatic: Men in peril entrusted themselves to him and he hid them.

sentences.zh: 與其好合，傾身無吝。

translations.literal: With those he favored he joined wholeheartedly without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: With friends he gave himself fully and generously.

sentences.zh: 若有相乖忤，便即疵毀，乃至聲色，加以謗罵。

translations.literal: If there was mutual discord he immediately found fault and destroyed them, even with voice and color, adding slander and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: When relations soured he reviled them loudly and abusively.

sentences.zh: 性又躁隘，至於論難之際，高聲攘振，無儒者之風。

translations.literal: By nature he was also irascible and narrow; in debate he raised his voice and clamored, without the bearing of a ru scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Irascible in debate, he shouted without scholarly decorum.

sentences.zh: 每語人云：「但道我好，雖知妄言，故勝道惡。

translations.literal: He often told people, "Just say I am good—even though you know it is false speech, still it beats saying evil."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Call me good—even false praise beats speaking ill."

sentences.zh: 」務進忌前，不顧後患，時人以此惡之。

translations.literal: He strove to advance and hated those before him, heedless of later trouble—men of the time hated him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious and jealous, heedless of consequences—contemporaries disliked him for it.

sentences.zh: 至於學術精微，當時莫及。

translations.literal: Yet in the subtlety of learning none of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarly depth none of his age matched him.

sentences.zh: 子崇祖，武定中，太尉外兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Chongzu in the Wuding era served as Outer Corps Adjutant to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongzu in Wuding was outer corps adjutant to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 崇祖弟遵祖，太昌中，業興傳其長子伯以授之。

translations.literal: Chongzu's younger brother Zunzu in the Taichang era—Yexing transmitted his eldest son's title of Baron to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang, Yexing passed his eldest son's baronial title to Zunzu, Chongzu's brother.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent ranks were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, ranks were reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古語云：容體不足觀，勇力不足恃，族姓不足道，先祖不足稱，然而顯聞四方，流聲後裔者，其惟學乎。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: An old saying runs, 'Physique is not worth viewing, courage and strength not worth relying on, clan name not worth mentioning, forebears not worth praising—yet those who shine famous in the four quarters and leave sound for posterity— is it not learning?'
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: An old proverb holds that body, courage, clan, and ancestors count for little—yet fame that reaches the four quarters and outlives a man comes from learning alone.

sentences.zh: 信哉斯言也。

translations.literal: How true are these words.
translations.idiomatic: How true that is.

sentences.zh: 梁越之徒，篤志不倦，自求諸己，遂能聞道下風，稱珍席上，或聚徒千百，或服冕乘軒，咸稽古之力也。

translations.literal: Men like Liang and Yue, with steadfast will unwearied, seeking within themselves, were able to hear the Way downwind, to be treasures on the mat, or gather hundreds and thousands of disciples, or wear crowns and ride chariots—all through the power of examining antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars like Liang and Yue, tireless in self-cultivation, won renown, disciples, and office through mastery of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十四 諸本目錄此卷注「不全」，卷末有宋人校語云：「高氏小史儒林傳無刁沖、盧景裕、李同軌三人，史目錄皆有之。

translations.literal: Various editions of Book of Wei juan 84 note in the table of contents that this juan is 'incomplete'; at the juan's end a Song collator's note says: 'Gao's Brief History Confucian Scholars lacks the three men Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui, while the History's table of contents lists all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Editions of Wei shu 84 mark the juan 'incomplete'; a Song note says Gao's Brief History lacks Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui though the catalogue lists them.

sentences.zh: 此卷刁沖、盧景裕傳全錄北史，非魏收書，史臣論亦出北史，北史全用隋書傳論。

translations.literal: In this juan the biographies of Diao Chong and Lu Jingyu are wholly copied from the History of the North, not Wei Shou's book; the historiographer's discussion also comes from the North History, which wholly uses the Sui History discussion of biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Here Diao Chong and Lu Jingyu are full North History copies, not Wei Shou; the historian's comment likewise comes from North History, which draws on Sui shu's biographical discussions.

sentences.zh: 」殿本以校語入考證，開頭一句又改成「魏收書儒林傳亡，用高氏小史補之」。

translations.literal: The Palace Edition entered the collation note into textual verification and changed the opening sentence to 'Wei Shou's Confucian Scholars is lost; supplemented from Gao's Brief History.'
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition incorporated the note into verification and rewrote the opening as 'Wei Shou's Ru lin zhuan is lost, supplemented from Gao's Brief History.'

sentences.zh: 按此卷常爽、刁沖、盧景裕、李同軌四傳，北史卷八一儒林傳所無。

translations.literal: According to this juan, the four biographies of Chang Shuang, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui are absent from History of the North juan 81 Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui are missing from North History 81 Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 常爽，北史卷四二有專傳，刁沖附卷二六刁雍傳，盧景裕附卷三０盧同傳，李同軌附卷三三李義深傳。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang has a separate biography in History of the North juan 42; Diao Chong is appended to juan 26 Diao Yong; Lu Jingyu to juan 30 Lu Tong; Li Tonggui to juan 33 Li Yishen.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang has North History 42; the others appear as appendices elsewhere in North History.

sentences.zh: 今檢此卷常爽傳也全同北史，宋人漏舉。

translations.literal: On examination this juan's Chang Shuang biography is also wholly the same as the North History—the Song collator omitted mentioning it.
translations.idiomatic: This juan's Chang Shuang also matches North History entirely—the Song note omitted it.

sentences.zh: 李同軌則魏書本已附卷三六李順傳，與此卷同軌傳幾乎全同，一人二傳，實為重出

translations.literal: Li Tonggui was already appended in Wei shu juan 36 Li Shun; nearly identical to this juan's Tonggui biography—one man, two biographies, truly duplicated
translations.idiomatic: Li Tonggui already appears in Wei shu 36 Li Shun—virtually duplicate with this biography.

sentences.zh: 〈北史同軌傳較簡〉

translations.literal: 〈North History Tonggui biography is briefer〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈North History Tonggui biography is briefer〉

sentences.zh: 其他諸傳，凡北史儒林傳所有諸人都比北史詳備。

translations.literal: The other biographies, for all persons also in North History Confucian Scholars, are more detailed than the North History.
translations.idiomatic: Other shared figures are more detailed here than in North History.

sentences.zh: 其中徐遵明傳，北史多出勒索學生事，李業興傳多出語音不正和與孫騰、邢子才對答語，當是北史據其他材料增入，非魏書原文所有。

translations.literal: Among them, Xu Zunming's biography in North History adds the matter of extorting students; Li Yexing's adds incorrect pronunciation and exchanges with Sun Teng and Xing Zicai—likely North History additions from other materials, not original Wei shu text.
translations.idiomatic: North History adds Xu Zunming's extortion and Li Yexing's speech quirks—likely later insertions.

sentences.zh: 傳序也像是北史傳序敍魏事一段所本。

translations.literal: The preface to the biographies also seems to be what the North History preface's Wei section was based on.
translations.idiomatic: The biographical preface seems to underlie North History's Wei section.

sentences.zh: 據上述情況，除常、刁、盧三傳及史論外，似皆魏書原文。

translations.literal: From the above, apart from the Chang, Diao, and Lu three biographies and the historian's discussion, all seems to be original Wei shu text.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Chang, Diao, Lu, and the historian's comment, the rest appears to be original Wei shu.

sentences.zh: 宋人於目錄注「不全」，於校語只說刁、盧二傳「非魏收書」，史臣論「出北史」，則也認為序和其他諸傳是魏書原文。

translations.literal: The Song men noted 'incomplete' in the catalogue; in the collation note they said only the Diao and Lu two biographies were 'not Wei Shou's book' and the historian's discussion 'from North History'—thus they also held the preface and other biographies to be original Wei shu.
translations.idiomatic: Song collators deemed only Diao and Lu non-Wei Shou; they treated the preface and other lives as original.

sentences.zh: 且據校語，當時比對高氏小史，只說三傳此有彼無，沒有說其他諸傳以小史補。

translations.literal: And according to the note, when comparing Gao's Brief History they said only that these three biographies exist here but not there—they did not say other biographies were supplemented from the Brief History.
translations.idiomatic: Comparison with Gao's Brief History noted only the three missing there, not other supplements.

sentences.zh: 小史久亡，清人又何從知之？

translations.literal: The Brief History has long been lost—how could Qing scholars have known?
translations.idiomatic: The Brief History is lost—Qing scholars could not verify.

sentences.zh: 但也有可疑之處：一，若說此卷只是殘缺不全，除三傳外均魏書原文，何以所缺前後錯出，恰好是北史儒林傳所無之傳？

translations.literal: Yet there are also doubtful points: first, if this juan is merely incomplete and apart from the three biographies all is original Wei shu, why are the missing parts scattered before and after, exactly the biographies absent from North History Confucian Scholars?
translations.idiomatic: If only incomplete, why do gaps align exactly with biographies missing from North History?

sentences.zh: 高氏小史節錄魏書，何以小史儒林傳所無的三傳也是北史儒林傳所無？

translations.literal: Gao's Brief History abridges Wei shu—why are the three biographies absent from Brief History Confucian Scholars also absent from North History Confucian Scholars?
translations.idiomatic: Why do the three missing from Brief History also lack North History Confucian entries?

sentences.zh: 二，李同軌，魏書已附李順傳，儒林傳目應無其名，何以校語說「史目錄有之」？

translations.literal: Second, Li Tonggui was already appended in Li Shun's biography—Confucian Scholars catalogue should not list his name—why does the note say 'the History catalogue lists it'?
translations.idiomatic: Li Tonggui was already under Li Shun—why does the catalogue list him separately?

sentences.zh: 或此所謂「史目錄」乃指宗諫史目等

translations.literal: Perhaps this 'History catalogue' refers to Zong Jian's History Catalogue and the like
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps 'History catalogue' means Zong Jian's catalogue

sentences.zh: 〈見卷八六孝感傳按語〉

translations.literal: 〈see the note to juan 86 Filial Conduct biographies〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈see juan 86 Filial Conduct note〉

sentences.zh: ，則後人據目補傳，何以不據本書目錄而據他書？

translations.literal: , then later men supplemented biographies according to the catalogue—why rely on other books rather than this book's catalogue?
translations.idiomatic: —then why supplement from other catalogues rather than this book's?

sentences.zh: 後人既已從李順傳中析出同軌傳入儒林，何以不刪李順傳中所有？

translations.literal: Later men having extracted Tonggui's biography from Li Shun into Confucian Scholars, why not delete what was in Li Shun's biography?
translations.idiomatic: Having split Tonggui into Confucian Scholars, why leave the duplicate under Li Shun?

sentences.zh: 這些疑問頗難解釋。

translations.literal: These questions are quite hard to explain.
translations.idiomatic: These problems resist easy explanation.

sentences.zh: 河間邢祐 諸本「祐」作「祜」，北史卷八一平恒傳作「祐」。

translations.literal: Xing You of Hejian: in various editions 'You' is written 'Hu'; History of the North juan 81 Ping Heng biography has 'You.'
translations.idiomatic: Xing You of Hejian: editions read Hu; North History 81 has You.

sentences.zh: 按邢祐附本書卷六五、北史卷四三邢巒傳，都作「祐」。

translations.literal: Xing You is appended in this book juan 65 and North History juan 43 Xing Luan biography—both have 'You.'
translations.idiomatic: Appendices in this book 65 and North History 43 Xing Luan also have You.

sentences.zh: 「祜」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: 'Hu' is a corrupt character; now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Hu is erroneous; corrected to You.

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: Same below.
translations.idiomatic: Same below.

sentences.zh: 燕東部侯釐 通鑑卷九八

translations.literal: Marquis Director of the East of Yan: Comprehensive Mirror juan 98
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Director of the East of Yan: Zizhi tongjian juan 98

sentences.zh: 〈三一０四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3104〉

sentences.zh: 見燕「中部俟釐慕輿句」。

translations.literal: has Yan 'Central Director Marquis Murong Ju.'
translations.idiomatic: has Yan 'Central Director Marquis Murong Ju.'

sentences.zh: 晉書卷一一０慕容儁載記無文，通鑑當據十六國春秋或范享燕書。

translations.literal: Jin shu juan 110 Murong Jun annals has no such text; the Comprehensive Mirror likely draws on Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms or Fan Xiang's Book of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin shu 110 lacks this; the Mirror likely uses Sixteen Kingdoms or Fan Xiang's Yan shu.

sentences.zh: 按突厥官有「俟利發」，契丹有「夷離堇」，並即此「俟釐」，這裏「侯」字當是「俟」的形訛。

translations.literal: Turkic offices have 'irkin' and Khitan have 'yilijin'—both are this 'irkin'; here 'hou' is likely a graphic corruption of 'yi' (transmitted as the homophone 'hou').
translations.idiomatic: Turkic irkin and Khitan yilijin match this irkin; the character written hou is likely a corruption of yi (the graph for 'irkin').

sentences.zh: 見臯魚之歎方歸而養親 諸本「臯」作「旱」。

translations.literal: Seeing Gao Yu's sigh then returning to nurture parents: in various editions 'Gao' is written 'Han.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu's sigh before returning to nurture parents: editions read Han for Gao.

sentences.zh: 北史卷八一劉獻之傳南本、殿本「旱」作「臯」。

translations.literal: History of the North juan 81 Liu Xianzhi biography in Southern and Palace editions has 'Han' as 'Gao.'
translations.idiomatic: North History 81 Liu Xianzhi: southern and palace editions read Gao.

sentences.zh: 按臯魚事見韓詩外傳卷九，云「於是門人辭歸而養親者十有三人」，與此傳語合。

translations.literal: The Gao Yu story is in Han shi waizhuan juan 9, saying 'thereupon thirteen disciples took leave to return and nurture parents,' matching this biography's wording.
translations.idiomatic: Han shi waizhuan 9 tells of thirteen disciples leaving to nurture parents—matching this text.

sentences.zh: 「旱」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: 'Han' is corrupt; now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Han is erroneous; corrected to Gao.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍 北史卷八一孫惠蔚傳無「大將軍」三字。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General: North History juan 81 Sun Huiwei biography lacks the three characters 'Grand General.'
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous Grand General: North History 81 Sun Huiwei lacks those three characters.

sentences.zh: 按大將軍甚重，以崔亮、崔光之顯貴，死後追贈亦只車騎、驃騎大將軍，孫惠蔚軍號為平東將軍，豈能驟贈此官。

translations.literal: Grand General is very weighty; even for the eminence of Cui Liang and Cui Guang, after death the retroactive grant was only General of Chariots and Cavalry or General of Agile Cavalry; Sun Huiwei's military title was General Who Pacifies the East—how could he suddenly receive this office?
translations.idiomatic: Grand general is exalted; even Cui Guang received only chariot or agile cavalry general—Sun Huiwei as pacifying-east general could hardly receive it.

sentences.zh: 疑是衍文，或「大」乃「本」之訛。

translations.literal: Suspected interpolation, or 'grand' is corruption of 'original.'
translations.idiomatic: Likely interpolation, or da (grand) corrupt for ben (original).

sentences.zh: 刺史河東裴植並徵沖為功曹 諸本和北史卷二六刁雍附刁沖傳「植」作「桓」。

translations.literal: Governor Pei Zhi of Hedong jointly summoned Chong as Merit Officer: in various editions and North History juan 26 Diao Yong appended Diao Chong biography 'Zhi' is written 'Huan.'
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi summoned Chong as merit officer: editions and North History 26 read Huan for Zhi.

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「『桓』當作『植』，植傳

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "'Huan' should be 'Zhi'; Zhi's biography
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai: Huan should be Zhi; see Zhi's biography

sentences.zh: 〈附卷七一裴叔業傳〉

translations.literal: 〈appended to juan 71 Pei Shuye biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈appended to juan 71 Pei Shuye〉

sentences.zh: 除瀛州刺史，即此時事。

translations.literal: appoints him Governor of Ying—this is the affair of that time.
translations.idiomatic: appoints him governor of Ying—at this time.

sentences.zh: 」按前劉蘭傳亦見瀛州刺史裴植。

translations.literal: According to the earlier Liu Lan biography Governor Pei Zhi of Ying is also seen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lan's biography also mentions Governor Pei Zhi of Ying.

sentences.zh: 刁沖稱勃海饒安人。

translations.literal: Diao Chong is styled a man of Rao'an in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Chong was from Rao'an in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六上地形志上滄州條和浮陽郡饒安條，熙平二年

translations.literal: Juan 106 part 1 Treatise on Geography, Yong Province entry and Fuyang Commandery Rao'an entry—in the second year of Xiping
translations.idiomatic: Geography 106, Yong and Fuyang Rao'an—in Xiping year two

sentences.zh: 〈五一七〉
分置滄州前，饒安屬瀛州浮陽郡，其稱「勃海」，乃因漢晉舊屬。

translations.literal: before Yong Province was separately established, Rao'an belonged to Fuyang Commandery of Ying Province; the style 'Bohai' is because of Han and Jin old affiliation.
translations.idiomatic: before Yong Province was split, Rao'an was in Ying's Fuyang; 'Bohai' reflects Han-Jin affiliation.

sentences.zh: 裴植為瀛州刺史在熙平前，饒安是瀛州縣，刁沖是本州人，故得為功曹。

translations.literal: Pei Zhi as Governor of Ying was before Xiping; Rao'an was a county of Ying; Diao Chong was a native of that province—therefore he could serve as Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi governed Ying before Xiping; Rao'an was his county—Chong could be merit officer.

sentences.zh: 張說是，今改正。

translations.literal: Zhang's statement is correct; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang is correct; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 國子博士高涼及范陽盧道侃 張森楷云：「『涼』當作『諒』。

translations.literal: National University Erudite Gao Liang and Lu Daokan of Fanyang: Zhang Senkai says, "'Liang' (the graph for 'cool') should be 'Liang' (the graph for 'sincere')."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai argues the erudite's name should read Gao Liang (sincere), not Gao Liang (cool)—

sentences.zh: 據高佑傳

translations.literal: According to Gao You's biography
translations.idiomatic: per Gao You's biography

sentences.zh: ，佑孫諒為國子博士，在孝文、宣武間，與刁沖同時，當即其人。」

translations.literal: , You's grandson Liang was Erudite of the National University; between Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xuanwu, contemporaneous with Diao Chong—he must be this man."
translations.idiomatic: , Gao You's grandson Liang served as national university erudite under Xiaowen and Xuanwu alongside Diao Chong—surely the same person."

sentences.zh: 初元顥入洛 諸本無「初」字，北史卷三０盧同附盧景裕傳有。

translations.literal: At first when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang: various editions lack the character 'first'; History of the North juan 30 Lu Tong appended Lu Jingyu biography has it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao first entered Luoyang: editions omit the word 'first'; North History 30 Lu Jingyu has it.

sentences.zh: 元顥事在前，前文敍事已至東魏末高澄當國時，李慈銘、張森楷均謂有誤。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao's affair comes earlier; the narrative above already reaches the end of Eastern Wei when Gao Cheng held power—Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both say this is an error.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao belongs earlier; the text already reaches Gao Cheng's era—Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai deem this misplaced.

sentences.zh: 李且謂「除國子博士前已載之，何必複出，北史於『元顥』上加一『初』字亦非。

translations.literal: Li moreover said, "Appointment as Erudite of the National University was already recorded before—why repeat it? Adding 'first' before 'Yuan Hao' in North History is also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Li also said the national university post was already recorded—repeating it is redundant; North History's added chu is wrong too.

sentences.zh: 」按這是追敍以前官位升退，刁沖「未曾有得失之色」，本非記歷官。

translations.literal: According to this it is retrospective narration of earlier office and promotion; Diao Chong's 'never showed color of gain or loss' was not meant as an official career record.
translations.idiomatic: This is flashback to earlier appointments; 'never showing gain or loss' is not a formal office list.

sentences.zh: 此傳本出北史，乃是脫「初」字，遂似敍事顛倒，今據補。

translations.literal: This biography originally came from North History; the loss of 'first' makes the narrative seem reversed—now supplemented accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The biography derives from North History; dropping chu reversed the sequence—now restored.

sentences.zh: 成戊子曆 按卷一０七律曆志載崔光表云：「總合九家，共成一曆，元起壬子，律始黃鍾。

translations.literal: Completion of the Wuzi calendar: according to juan 107 Treatise on Pitch Pipes and Calendars, Cui Guang's memorial says, "Combining the nine households into one calendar, origin at ren-zi, pitch beginning at yellow bell."
translations.idiomatic: On the Wuzi calendar: Treatise 107 cites Cui Guang combining nine schools into one calendar starting ren-zi with yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 」業興初造之曆起於戊子，為戊子曆，至是「總合九家」則起於壬子，為壬子曆。

translations.literal: Yexing's originally devised calendar began at wu-zi, the Wuzi calendar; when 'the nine households were combined' it began at ren-zi, the Renzi calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing's first calendar began at wu-zi; the combined nine-household version began at ren-zi.

sentences.zh: 卷八二常景傳亦稱「先是參議正光壬子曆」可證。

translations.literal: Chang Jing's biography in juan 82 also says 'earlier participating in discussion of the Zheng guang Renzi calendar'—this can verify.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing's biography (juan 82) mentions the Zheng guang Renzi calendar—confirming this.

sentences.zh: 這裏「戊子」乃「壬子」之訛。

translations.literal: Here 'wu-zi' is a corruption of 'ren-zi.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu-zi here is a corruption of ren-zi.

sentences.zh: 與兼散騎常侍李諧 諸本脫「散」字，今據北史卷八一李業興傳補。

translations.literal: With Concurrent Regular Palace Attendant Li Xie: various editions omit the character 'san' (cadre); now supplemented from History of the North juan 81 Li Yexing biography.
translations.idiomatic: With concurrent regular palace attendant Li Xie: editions drop san (cadre); restored from North History 81.

sentences.zh: 久矣夫予之不託於音也 諸本此句作「久矣，不託音」。

translations.literal: 'Long has it been since I was not entrusted to music': various editions read this line as 'Long has it been—not entrusted to music.'
translations.idiomatic: The line 'Long has it been since I was not entrusted to music' appears in editions as the shorter 'Long has it been—not entrusted to music.'
